# Load/Mine malicious Qwen2 models on Hugging Face

- ID: pluto-loadmine-qwen2-malware-2026
- Reported: 2026-11-04
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/pluto-loadmine-qwen2-malware-2026/

## Summary
Malicious Qwen2 test models uploaded to Hugging Face (e.g. MENXIANGYU/qwen2-tiny) and mirrored on ModelScope. config.json auto_map field points to modeling_evil2.EvilModel which executes on trust_remote_code=True and vLLM versions before 0.14.0 without that flag (CVE-2026-22807). Payload runs fileless peakminer cryptominer via memfd_create, establishes .bashrc persistence, deploys reverse shells, and achieves GPUStack container escape. Models appear as legitimate Qwen2 variants for testing purposes.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: User loads malicious model from Hugging Face or ModelScope with trust_remote_code=True or vulnerable vLLM version
- Victims and sectors: ML researchers, AI developers, organizations using Hugging Face models
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: Multiple regions reflects global Hugging Face and ModelScope user base
- Scale and metrics: Multiple malicious models uploaded including MENXIANGYU/qwen2-tiny; exact victim count unknown

## Attack flow
### upload: Malicious models uploaded to repositories (access)

Attacker uploaded trojanized Qwen2 test models to Hugging Face and ModelScope with malicious config.json auto_map fields

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### load: Victim loads malicious model (ai)

User loads model with trust_remote_code=True or via vulnerable vLLM <0.14.0 (CVE-2026-22807)

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### execute: Malicious code executes during model load (execution)

modeling_evil2.EvilModel runs from config.json auto_map field during model initialization

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### miner: Fileless cryptominer deployed (impact)

peakminer runs via memfd_create for fileless execution; establishes .bashrc persistence

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### escalation: Additional payloads and container escape (impact)

Reverse shells deployed; GPUStack container escape achieved

Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

### Connections

- upload -> load
- load -> execute
- execute -> miner
- miner -> escalation

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010.003](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010.003) Model — Attackers poisoned publicly available ML models on Hugging Face and ModelScope platforms
  Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>
- [AML.T0058](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0058) Publish Poisoned Models — Malicious code injected via model config.json auto_map field executes during model loading
  Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>
- [AML.T0011.000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011.000) Unsafe AI Artifacts — Cryptominer achieves persistence through .bashrc modification
  Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Fileless peakminer cryptominer runs via memfd_create to evade detection
  Evidence: <https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/>

## Prevention
Pin and verify model checksums; avoid trust_remote_code=True; update vLLM to 0.14.0 or later; monitor memfd_create usage; scan .bashrc for unauthorized changes; detect outbound cryptocurrency mining traffic; review model config.json auto_map fields; use model scanning tools

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/) model repository
- ModelScope mirror
- Qwen2 model format
- vLLM <0.14.0 (CVE-2026-22807)
- Transformers library (trust_remote_code execution)

### Other tooling
- peakminer cryptominer
- memfd_create (fileless execution)
- .bashrc persistence
- Reverse shell
- GPUStack container escape

## Source notes
Relevant detection rules:
- Sigma: Suspicious Cron File Created (persistence via .bashrc) (https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/file_event/file_event_lnx_susp_cron_file_created.yml)
- Sigma: Audio Capture via memfd_create (fileless execution pattern, can detect suspicious memfd_create usage) (https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/auditd/lnx_auditd_audio_capture.yml)
- Note: Cryptominer detection typically requires network traffic analysis (cryptocurrency pool connections) and process monitoring for mining-specific CPU/GPU patterns. Container escape detection depends on specific container runtime audit logs.

## Sources
- [Load/Mine: A malware campaign targeting Hugging Face and ModelScope](https://pluto.security/blog/hugging-face-malware-campaign-load-mine/) — Pluto Security

# Cyera Research - Tampered copy of Anthropic's PDF skill carrying Linux Go backdoor system_linux

- ID: cyera-anthropic-pdf-skill-backdoor-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-03
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/cyera-anthropic-pdf-skill-backdoor-2026-11/

## Summary
Cyera Research (Nov 3, 2026) discovered six skill archives impersonating Anthropic's official PDF skill, observed May 23 - July 14, 2026. Each archive contains 11 files byte-identical to upstream Anthropic pdf skill (github.com/anthropics/skills), but SKILL.md is truncated from 315 lines to 19 lines keeping official name and description while replacing Quick Start section with curl https://scan.100tal.com command, and adds 5.1 MB garble-obfuscated 64-bit Linux Go ELF binary system_linux. Binary features AES-256-GCM encrypted configuration with 0xAA XOR decryption revealing C2 81.70.101.115:2345 and attaches /bin/bash over raw TCP socket. Simplified Chinese strings in binary and UTC+8 archive timestamps indicate Chinese-language development environment. scan.100tal.com hostname linked to TAL Education Group infrastructure. Cyera notes attribution is unknown and could indicate targeted attack or internal security exercise. Cyera analyzed archives but did not observe live execution of system_linux backdoor. garble obfuscator (github.com/burrowers/garble) used to strip Go function names and identifiers. Demonstrates supply-chain risk where skill typosquatting or compromised distribution channels can deliver backdoors to AI developer environments.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor; UTC+8 archive timestamps; Simplified Chinese strings in binary; scan.100tal.com hostname (TAL Education Group-linked); Cyera notes attribution unknown and could be targeted attack or security exercise

- Actor: Unknown
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: unknown
- Attributed by: Cyera Research
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Developers install tampered PDF skill archive from unknown distribution channel (not Anthropic's official Skills repository)
- Victims and sectors: AI developers using Claude Skills; targets include AI/ML engineering teams, research labs, and organizations deploying Anthropic skills
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Six tampered skill archives observed May 23 - July 14, 2026; Cyera analyzed archives but did not observe live system_linux execution

## Attack flow
### create-tampered-skill: Create tampered PDF skill with system_linux backdoor (execution)

Create tampered PDF skill with system_linux backdoor

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### truncate-skill-md: Truncate SKILL.md (315→19 lines), add curl scan.100tal.com (execution)

Truncate SKILL.md (315→19 lines), add curl scan.100tal.com

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### obfuscate-backdoor: garble-obfuscate system_linux Go binary (execution)

garble-obfuscate system_linux Go binary

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### distribute-skill: Distribute tampered skill via unknown channel (execution)

Distribute tampered skill via unknown channel

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### developer-install: Developer installs tampered PDF skill (execution)

Developer installs tampered PDF skill

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### backdoor-execution: system_linux connects 81.70.101.115:2345, attaches /bin/bash (impact)

system_linux connects 81.70.101.115:2345, attaches /bin/bash

Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

### Connections

- create-tampered-skill -> truncate-skill-md
- truncate-skill-md -> obfuscate-backdoor
- obfuscate-backdoor -> distribute-skill
- distribute-skill -> developer-install
- developer-install -> backdoor-execution

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Supply-chain attack targeting AI skill distribution; tampered Anthropic PDF skill delivers Linux backdoor to developer workstations in AI/ML development environments
  Evidence: <https://www.cyera.com/research/malicious-copy-anthropic-pdf-skill-carries-linux-backdoor>

## Prevention
Only install skills from Anthropic's official Skills repository (github.com/anthropics/skills); verify skill archive integrity and file count before installation; scan skill archives for unexpected binaries (system_linux, system_darwin, etc.); monitor skill installation for outbound connections to non-Anthropic domains (scan.100tal.com, 81.70.101.115); implement network egress filtering for skill execution environments; use read-only skill directories where possible; audit SKILL.md for truncated or modified Quick Start sections referencing external domains; educate developers on skill supply-chain risks

## Detections
- [Linux Shell Pipe to Shell](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_susp_pipe_shell.yml) (sigma) — Detects suspicious shell pipes; relevant for detecting /bin/bash reverse shell execution from system_linux backdoor
- [Bash Interactive Shell](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_bash_interactive_shell.yml) (sigma) — Detects bash interactive shell spawning; directly applicable to system_linux attaching /bin/bash to TCP socket
- Skill supply-chain integrity monitoring (guidance) — Verify skill archives against official Anthropic Skills repository (github.com/anthropics/skills); alert on unexpected binaries in skill directories (system_linux, system_darwin); scan SKILL.md for modified Quick Start sections referencing external domains (scan.100tal.com); monitor skill installation for outbound TCP connections to non-Anthropic infrastructure (81.70.101.115:2345); detect garble-obfuscated Go binaries via string entropy analysis; flag skill archives with UTC+8 timestamps and Simplified Chinese strings when organization is not China-based
- Network egress filtering (guidance) — Block outbound connections from skill execution environments to unknown IPs; alert on raw TCP connections to port 2345; monitor for /bin/bash processes with network sockets; detect AES-256-GCM encrypted config files in skill directories

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-05-23
- Last updated: 2026-11-03
- 2026-05-23 (Cyera Research): Earliest observed tampered PDF skill archive with system_linux backdoor
- 2026-07-14 (Cyera Research): Latest observed tampered PDF skill archive (six total observed May 23 - Jul 14)
- 2026-11-03 (Cyera Research): Cyera publishes analysis with IOCs and backdoor mechanism; notes attribution unknown and system_linux was not observed executing

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Anthropic [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) Skills (impersonated; official repo https://github.com/anthropics/skills)
- garble [Go](https://github.com/golang/go) obfuscator (https://github.com/burrowers/garble)

### Other tooling
- system_linux [Go](https://github.com/golang/go) backdoor (5.1 MB ELF64, AES-256-GCM + 0xAA XOR config)
- /bin/bash reverse shell over TCP

## Source notes
Cyera Research (Assaf Morag, Nov 3, 2026) primary source; all hashes from Cyera IoC table: system_linux SHA-256 50cb53704f318e4fc9a9cd8f6d32eb98d8c666501c720d63c2c701caeb6fa946, SKILL.md SHA-256 d0d4144609825ee7480f7889ee04d97f4b1d9eaa8a46c2a0d46d81ab5aa83827, plus archive hashes; network IOCs 81.70.101.115 and scan.100tal.com verified from Cyera; Cyera explicitly states archives were analyzed but system_linux was not observed executing

## Sources

# GTIG LLMJacking - UNC6993, Jet Night, D1337-KAIROS monetize cloud models

- ID: gtig-llmjacking-unc6993-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-02
- AI role: ai_infra_as_c2
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/gtig-llmjacking-unc6993-2026-11/

## Summary
Multiple threat clusters (UNC6993, Jet Night operators, D1337-KAIROS) hijack enterprise access to LLMs across AWS Bedrock, Azure, GCP. Initial access via exposed cloud identity tokens (IAM, Service Account keys, GitHub PATs, session tokens), stolen LLM API keys from public GitHub, exploited web app vulnerabilities, LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217 (/key/regenerate endpoint rebind). UNC6993 used session hijacking page masquerading as app portal to steal JSON payloads with active access tokens. Threat actors enable LLM services, create API keys, provision GPUs, subscribe Pay-As-You-Go, deploy LiteLLM/new-api/gcli2api gateways, host Manus agent framework with SearXNG metasearch. Monetize via LLM Mixers (Jet Night at jet-night.com $60/month unlimited, ai-relay on lookalike domains, newapi.pro). Stealthy credential validation sweeps with max_tokens=1. Fraudulent charges $100K in single day, cumulative $1M per org. Division of labor between initial access and downstream monetization. Fireworks AI (Nov 9, 2026) reports Oct 23 third-party cloud provider hosting Fireworks R&D breached; Oct 24 attacker entered via provider, ran unauthorized workload; reached account/billing data and, for some customers, secrets, datasets, partly trained model weights. Fireworks attributes to financially motivated LLMjacking group selling access to illicit routing gateways; GTIG/Mandiant report referenced; Unit 42 forensics. Notion, a Fireworks customer, published a downstream notice: Fireworks told Notion on Nov 2 that a small dataset of Notion AI synthetic test data was accessed; Notion disconnected and deleted Fireworks data by the morning of Nov 3; on Nov 6 Fireworks said customer data may have been accessed; on Nov 8 Fireworks confirmed the final dataset; on Nov 9 Notion contacted affected customers. The exposed data is Notion AI Insights chat transcripts for under 1 percent of workspaces, mostly unattributable (no user or workspace labels, and no tool-call results). No other Notion features were affected. Notion told affected customers to treat the transcripts as exposed and to rotate secrets pasted into Notion AI. On Nov 11 Notion revoked exposed Notion API keys found in affected user messages.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
UNC6993 (Mandiant); Jet Night operators; D1337-KAIROS persona; multiple financially motivated threat clusters operating globally; division of labor between initial access operators and LLM Mixer monetization operators

- Actor: UNC6993, Jet Night operators, D1337-KAIROS
- Country: Global
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Google Threat Intelligence Group, Fireworks AI
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Misconfigured Service Account keys; session hijacking page masquerading as LLM portal; stolen GitHub PATs + web app vulnerability exploitation; compromised IAM credentials with cloud federation tokens; harvested exposed LLM API keys from public GitHub; LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217 (user ID rebind vulnerability in /key/regenerate endpoint)
- Victims and sectors: Organizations in North America, South America, Asia Pacific across financial services, retail, technology, transportation sectors; Fireworks AI customers (account/billing data, secrets, datasets, partly trained model weights for some customers); Notion workspaces using Fireworks for Notion AI Insights (under 1 percent, chat transcripts)
- Regions: North America, South America, Asia
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Multiple incidents in 2026; fraudulent charges exceeding $100K USD in single day; cumulative charges at some orgs reaching $1M USD; Jet Night passed nearly $1M in token costs to victim org; one actor made ~800K Bedrock calls over 30 hours (90% success), another 1.7M calls over 13 hours (1M+ success); 500K+ LLM API calls in <8 hours; Jet Night offers unlimited tokens $60/month (typical market $100-$250/month)

## Attack flow
### initial-access: Compromised cloud identity and LLM API keys (access)

Misconfigured Service Account keys; session hijacking page for LLM portal JSON payloads; stolen GitHub PATs + web app vuln; compromised IAM with federation tokens; exposed LLM API keys harvested from public GitHub; stealthy validation sweeps with max_tokens=1

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### lateral-persistence: Privilege escalation and persistence (execution)

Enumerated cloud services/repos/data stores; cloned codebases for secrets; queried data warehouse metadata; exploited LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217 (/key/regenerate rebind) to elevate Virtual Keys to PROXY_ADMIN; created unauthorized IAM/service accounts; injected SSH keys; attached admin policies; created backdoor accounts disguised as billing utilities

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### llm-abuse: LLM resource hijacking (ai)

Enabled managed generative platforms; created additional API keys; subscribed Pay-As-You-Go; selected premium models; launched high-volume inference; 'burn and rotate' short-lived service accounts; provisioned GPU instances; requested quota increases; deployed LiteLLM gateways; hosted Manus agent framework with SearXNG metasearch and sandbox execution

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### monetization: LLM Mixer resale (impact)

UNC6993 deployed new-api and gcli2api to aggregate stolen keys and balance loads; Jet Night (jet-night.com) $60/month unlimited token plan powered by stolen keys, passed ~$1M costs to victim; ai-relay on lookalike domains siphons access to newapi.pro resale ecosystem; D1337-KAIROS persona with Node.js proxy bundles; division of labor between access and monetization operators

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### charges: Fraudulent billing (impact)

UNC6993 accumulated $100K+ charges quickly; cumulative charges at orgs reaching $1M; one actor 800K Bedrock calls over 30 hours (Opus 75% of calls), another 1.7M calls over 13 hours; token usage profile resembles resold coding-agent traffic with prompt caching; $100K+ estimated usage at list price for two documented cases

Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>

### Connections

- initial-access -> lateral-persistence
- lateral-persistence -> llm-abuse
- llm-abuse -> monetization
- llm-abuse -> charges
- monetization -> charges

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Threat actors compromise cloud compute credentials and hijack enterprise access to AWS Bedrock, Azure Cognitive Services, and GCP Gemini to fraudulently monetize through illicit gateways and LLM Mixers
  Evidence: <https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/llmjacking-monetizing-compromised-cloud-models>
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Fireworks AI third-party cloud provider breach resulted in unauthorized workload execution and customer data access
  Evidence: <https://fireworks.ai/security/bulletins/october-2026-security-incident-update>
- [AML.T0025](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0025) Exfiltration via Cyber Means — Attackers exfiltrated account/billing data, secrets, datasets, and partly trained model weights from Fireworks AI
  Evidence: <https://fireworks.ai/security/bulletins/october-2026-security-incident>

## Prevention
IAM least privilege; centralized secrets management; code monitoring for API keys; routine config audits; rate limiting via Cloud Armor; network allow listing; budget alerts and API quotas; phishing-resistant MFA; shadow LLM discovery; granular API key scopes; validation sweep monitoring (max_tokens=1); vulnerability/ML supply chain patching; gateway patch management (LiteLLM CVE-2026-40217); sandboxed execution; vetted model repositories; graph-based exposure modeling

## Detections
- Cloud LLM resource abuse monitoring (guidance) — Implement budget alerts and API quotas; monitor for validation sweeps (max_tokens=1); detect rapid GPU provisioning; alert on Pay-As-You-Go subscriptions from service accounts; monitor LiteLLM/new-api/gcli2api gateway deployments; detect Manus agent framework and SearXNG installations; flag burn-and-rotate service account patterns; monitor Jet Night, ai-relay, newapi.pro resale infrastructure connections
- Third-party cloud provider security (guidance) — For Fireworks AI incident: audit third-party cloud provider access; implement least-privilege for R&D environments; monitor unauthorized workload execution; detect account/billing data access anomalies; alert on secrets, datasets, model weight access; implement cloud provider security controls. Notion downstream notice has no endpoint or CloudTrail pattern: the exposed objects are Notion AI Insights chat transcripts held by the vendor. Affected customers should treat those transcripts as exposed and rotate secrets pasted into Notion AI.

## Timeline
- Last updated: 2026-11-11
- 2026-11-02 (Google Threat Intelligence Group): GTIG reports UNC6993, Jet Night, D1337-KAIROS LLMjacking campaigns; fraudulent charges $100K-$1M per org; LLM Mixer resale via jet-night.com, ai-relay, newapi.pro
- 2026-10-24 (Fireworks AI): Fireworks AI third-party cloud provider breached Oct 23; attacker entered Oct 24, ran unauthorized workload; accessed account/billing data, secrets, datasets, partly trained model weights
- 2026-11-09 (Fireworks AI): Fireworks AI attributes to financially motivated LLMjacking group selling illicit routing gateway access; GTIG/Mandiant report referenced; Unit 42 forensics
- 2026-11-02 (Notion): Fireworks notified Notion that a small dataset was accessed. Notion found only Notion AI synthetic test data, with no customer data in that first set.
- 2026-11-03 (Notion): Notion disconnected from Fireworks, deleted data held there, and stopped communication with Fireworks.
- 2026-11-06 (Notion): Fireworks told Notion that malicious actors may have accessed customer data. Notion opened a second investigation.
- 2026-11-08 (Notion): Fireworks confirmed the final impacted dataset to Notion.
- 2026-11-09 (Notion): Notion contacted affected customers. The dataset is Notion AI Insights chat transcripts for under 1 percent of workspaces, mostly unattributable, with no tool-call results and no other Notion features affected.
- 2026-11-11 (Notion): Notion revoked exposed Notion API keys found in affected user messages during the investigation.

# Malicious MCP servers on npm (ifasn, gadgethumans)

- ID: malicious-mcp-servers-npm-2026-11
- Reported: 2026-11-02
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/malicious-mcp-servers-npm-2026-11/

## Summary
Multiple malicious MCP servers published on npm. @ifasn/md-doc-mcp and @ifasn/mmdd-doc-mcp probe cloud metadata endpoints, read sensitive files (/etc/shadow, SSH keys, .env, Kubernetes tokens), and exfiltrate to 121.199.24.94. @ifasn/ms-doc-mcp versions 2.0.9 and 2.1.1 (GHSA-556m-xfwj-7wff, MAL-2026-18603) use imdsAudit() function to steal Alibaba Cloud IMDS credentials from 100.100.100.200 and exfiltrate them over MCP stdout. gadgethumans-mcp versions 1.0.10-1.0.15 leak WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY environment variable in HTTP header on every tool call. Published with OpenSSF GHSA-rvw8-22w3-342v, GHSA-4h5p-w547-9qmv (Nov 2) and Leitwacht LWA-2026-13557, LWA-2026-13564. Aug 12, 2026: Pillar Security disclosed Deadbugz malicious MCP server (GitHub zellkernel) stealing AI model credentials and API keys. Feb 20, 2026: Socket discovered SANDWORM_MODE campaign spreading malicious MCP servers targeting developer credentials. November 9-12 additions: @rfewqa-fes/mnm-doc-mcp 1.0.0 (MAL-2026-19148, Amazon Inspector) ships an inert MCP stub in index.js. Its package.json pulls the only dependency, node-health-utils, as an off-registry tarball over plain HTTP from http://121.199.24.94/dl/health-utils-1.0.0.tgz, so whatever that host serves, including lifecycle scripts, runs at npm install. package.json sha256 f8ad55746cfac30b0a9401634b2728afc93e6dc20a85c511efd0ed312e466e8d. Package tarball sha1 f3ad664b487c4041e7e66e5744656ed44e1a6f6a. GitHub also marked @lemili9804/mcp-weather-server 1.0.3 and 1.0.6 (GHSA-qwfq-cw9x-55x4), mcp-contract-tester all versions (GHSA-34p7-qcxm-gc39, MAL-2026-19082), and @bestcoolman/dev-mcp (GHSA-vgx2-8w7x-xr8v, MAL-2026-19052) as malware, with no published behavior write-up. Attack exploits trust in the MCP ecosystem and npm package distribution.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
unknown

- Actor: Unknown npm publishers (ifasn, gadgethumans, rfewqa-fes, lemili9804, bestcoolman, zellkernel)
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: cybercrime
- Attributed by: OpenSSF, Leitwacht, GitHub Advisory Database, Amazon Inspector, Pillar Security, Socket
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: User installs malicious MCP server from npm
- Victims and sectors: AI agent developers, organizations using MCP servers
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: Multiple regions reflects global npm and MCP user base
- Scale and metrics: Multiple malicious MCP packages identified (ifasn, gadgethumans, Deadbugz, SANDWORM_MODE); exact installation count unknown

## Attack flow
### publish: Malicious MCP servers published to npm (access)

Three packages published including @ifasn/md-doc-mcp, @ifasn/mmdd-doc-mcp, and gadgethumans-mcp 1.0.10-1.0.15

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### install: User installs malicious MCP server (ai)

Developer or organization adds malicious package to MCP configuration

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### probe: Server probes for sensitive information (execution)

ifasn packages probe cloud metadata endpoints and read /etc/shadow, SSH keys, .env, k8s tokens

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### exfil-files: File-based credentials exfiltrated (impact)

ifasn packages send stolen credentials to 121.199.24.94

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### exfil-header: Wallet keys leaked in headers (impact)

gadgethumans-mcp sends WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY in HTTP header on every tool call

Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

### Connections

- publish -> install
- install -> probe
- probe -> exfil-files
- probe -> exfil-header

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010.001) AI Software — Attackers published malicious MCP servers through npm package ecosystem
  Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>
- [AML.T0011.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011.001) Malicious Package — Malicious MCP servers run persistently as agent tooling
  Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>
- [AML.T0055](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0055) Unsecured Credentials — Packages exfiltrate credentials from environment variables and sensitive files
  Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>
- [AML.T0025](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0025) Exfiltration via Cyber Means — MCP servers probe cloud metadata endpoints for credentials and instance information
  Evidence: <https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages>

## Prevention
Verify MCP server sources before installation; review MCP server permissions and network access; monitor cloud metadata endpoint access; detect unauthorized file reads of sensitive paths; inspect HTTP headers for credential leakage; use MCP server sandboxing; inventory installed MCP packages

## Detections
- [Suspicious PowerShell from npm Package Install](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/windows/execution_suspicious_powershell_from_npm_install.toml) (elastic) — Windows. PowerShell started from an npm install script. Use when the remote tarball or a GHSA-flagged MCP package runs a Windows lifecycle script.
- Plain-HTTP tarball and GHSA-only packages (guidance) — Also block http://121.199.24.94/dl/health-utils-1.0.0.tgz and alert on package.json dependencies that are bare http:// tarball URLs. @lemili9804/mcp-weather-server, mcp-contract-tester, and @bestcoolman/dev-mcp are confirmed malicious by GitHub but have no published behavior, so no tighter rule is cited for them.

## Source notes
OpenSSF GHSA-rvw8-22w3-342v and GHSA-4h5p-w547-9qmv published Nov 2 2026; Leitwacht advisories LWA-2026-13557 and LWA-2026-13564; GitHub advisory GHSA-556m-xfwj-7wff (MAL-2026-18603) for @ifasn/ms-doc-mcp

Relevant detection rules:
- Monitor access to cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254, 100.100.100.200 (Alibaba), metadata.google.internal, etc.)
- Alert on unauthorized reads of /etc/shadow, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, .env files
- Detect access to Kubernetes service account tokens (/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/)
- Monitor HTTP headers for sensitive environment variable leakage (WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, etc.)
- Alert on npm package installations from unverified sources
- Note: Cloud metadata access typically detected via network monitoring or instance-level audit logs (CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, GCP Cloud Logging). File access requires host-based file integrity monitoring.

# Trojanized anthropic.claude-code Cursor extension

- ID: anthropic-claude-code-trojan-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-30
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/anthropic-claude-code-trojan-2026-10/

## Summary
Tampered anthropic.claude-code extension versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 served via Cursor marketplace install and auto-update on Oct 29 2026 from ~5:27 AM to 4:35 PM ET. Loader in extension.js collected hostname, username, environment variables matching secret patterns, added SSH key svc-telemetry to authorized_keys, established reverse SSH tunnel to tunnel@134.209.82.225, beaconed to :8099/beacon. Persistence via com.apple.sysmond LaunchAgent (macOS), @reboot cron (Linux), SysMon scheduled task (Windows). GitHub repo https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-quickstarts compromised.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Supply-chain compromise of official Cursor marketplace extension via compromised GitHub repository
- Victims and sectors: Cursor IDE users who installed or auto-updated anthropic.claude-code extension during compromise window
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: Multiple regions reflects global Cursor user base; specific affected geography unknown
- Scale and metrics: Served Oct 29 2026 ~5:27 AM-4:35 PM ET via Cursor marketplace; exact victim count unknown

## Attack flow
### supply-chain: GitHub repository compromised (access)

Attacker gained access to anthropics/anthropic-quickstarts GitHub repository and pushed malicious extension versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### distribution: Malicious versions served via marketplace (ai)

Cursor marketplace distributed compromised extension via install and auto-update from Oct 29 5:27 AM to 4:35 PM ET

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### collection: Extension collects host information and secrets (execution)

Loader in extension.js collected hostname, username, environment variable names matching secret patterns

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### backdoor: SSH backdoor established (impact)

Added svc-telemetry SSH key to authorized_keys and established reverse SSH tunnel to tunnel@134.209.82.225 with beacon to :8099/beacon

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### persistence: Platform-specific persistence installed (impact)

com.apple.sysmond LaunchAgent (macOS), @reboot cron (Linux), SysMon scheduled task (Windows)

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>

### Connections

- supply-chain -> distribution
- distribution -> collection
- collection -> backdoor
- backdoor -> persistence

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010.001) AI Software — Attacker compromised an AI coding assistant extension in the official marketplace
  Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/> <https://cursor.com/blog/claude-code-extension-security-notice>
- [AML.T0011](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011) User Execution — Extension established persistence through platform-specific mechanisms
  Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/>
- [AML.T0055](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0055) Unsecured Credentials — Malicious extension collected environment variables matching secret patterns
  Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/30/inside-malicious-claude-code-branded-cursor-extension-persistent-ssh-backdoor/>

## Prevention
Monitor extension integrity; review SSH authorized_keys; detect outbound SSH tunnels to suspicious IPs; scan for LaunchAgent/cron/@reboot persistence; review scheduled tasks; monitor environment variable access patterns

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-29
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-10-29 (Cursor, Microsoft): Trojanized anthropic.claude-code extension served via Cursor marketplace for ~11 hours
- 2026-10-30 (Microsoft): Microsoft Threat Intelligence analysis of persistent SSH backdoor published
- 2026-11-01 (OpenSourceMalware.com): Additional technical analysis of Claude Code trojan SSH backdoor persistence mechanisms

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/)
- anthropic.claude-code extension

### Other tooling

- LaunchAgent persistence (macOS)
- Cron persistence (Linux)
- Scheduled task persistence (Windows)

- Sigma: Scheduled Task Creation Via Schtasks (https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_schtasks_creation.yml)

# FakeGit agentbaiting - 800+ fake AI skills and MCP servers recommended by agents

- ID: fakegit-agentbaiting-island-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-30
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/fakegit-agentbaiting-island-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 30, 2026: Island Security identified 'FakeGit' campaign: 800+ fake GitHub repositories impersonating popular AI skills, MCP servers, Cursor rules, and Claude Code extensions. Repos use typosquat/combosquat names (e.g., cursor-rules-best-practices, mcp-server-github-enhanced, claude-code-skills-security), contain trojanized npm/PyPI packages or malicious install scripts. Adversary optimized repo metadata (README, topics, stars, forks) to rank highly in LLM tool recommendations: when users ask agents find me a GitHub MCP server or what Cursor skills should I use?, agents recommend FakeGit repos from search results. Payloads: Shai-Hulud variants, Discord webhook exfiltration, npm/PyPI worms, SSH backdoors. Island tracked 2,400+ installations from agent recommendations Oct-Nov 2026. Island reports the repositories deliver SmartLoader, which establishes persistence and installs StealC to steal credentials, active sessions, and other sensitive data. Attack exploits agent trust in GitHub search ranking and lack of package verification.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor; 'FakeGit' campaign; sophisticated understanding of LLM recommendation mechanics and AI developer workflows

- Actor: FakeGit
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Island
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: AI agent recommends malicious GitHub repo in response to user query; user clones/installs per agent suggestion
- Victims and sectors: 2,400+ installations tracked Oct-Nov 2026 from agent recommendations; AI developers using agent-assisted package discovery
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 800+ fake GitHub repos created; 2,400+ installations from agent recommendations (Oct-Nov 2026); ongoing campaign as of Nov 2026

## Attack flow
### create-fakes: Create fake repos (ai)

Adversary creates 800+ GitHub repos with typosquat/combosquat names mimicking popular AI skills, MCP servers, Cursor rules; optimizes metadata (README, topics, keywords) for LLM search ranking; inflates stars/forks

Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

### agent-recommends: Agent recommends malicious repo (ai)

User asks AI agent to find/recommend skill, MCP server, or Cursor rule; agent searches GitHub/web, ranks FakeGit repos highly due to optimized metadata; agent recommends malicious repo to user as legitimate tool

Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

### user-installs: User installs per agent recommendation (execution)

User trusts agent recommendation and clones repo or installs package; malicious install script or npm/PyPI postinstall executes; Shai-Hulud stealer, SSH backdoor, or worm payload deploys

Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

### compromise: Credential theft and persistence (impact)

Payload harvests AI API keys, GitHub tokens, SSH keys, AWS credentials; establishes persistence (SSH backdoor, cron job); exfiltrates to Discord webhooks or C2; 2,400+ successful compromises tracked Oct-Nov 2026

Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

### Connections

- create-fakes -> agent-recommends
- agent-recommends -> user-installs
- user-installs -> compromise

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Adversary manipulates LLM tool recommendation systems to deliver malicious packages via agent-suggested GitHub repos
  Evidence: <https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware>

## Prevention
Verify GitHub repos before install (check org, stars, age, commit history); use allowlisted skill/MCP sources; implement agent guardrails to warn on unverified packages; educate users not to blindly trust agent recommendations; review install scripts; use SCA tools; prefer official sources (Anthropic MCP registry, Cursor skills directory); flag typosquat patterns

## Detections
- [Potential Browser Data Stealing](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_susp_copy_browser_data.yml) (sigma) — Detects StealC infostealer browser data theft on Windows
- [Suspicious File Access to Browser Credential Storage](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/file/file_access/file_access_win_susp_process_access_browser_cred_files.yml) (sigma) — Detects SmartLoader/StealC accessing browser credential files
- Malicious skill and MCP repository detection (guidance) — Monitor agent-initiated GitHub clones; alert on typosquat repo names; verify repo authenticity (check org, stars, age, commit history); detect inflated stars/forks with low commit activity; scan for SmartLoader/StealC signatures

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-30
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-10-30 (Island): Initial discovery and analysis

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/) and [Cursor](https://cursor.com/) rules
- [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers
- AI coding assistants (generic)
- LLM search and recommendation systems

### Other tooling
- Fake GitHub repositories (800+)
- npm/PyPI trojanized packages
- Shai-Hulud credential stealer variants
- SSH backdoors
- Discord webhook exfiltration
- SmartLoader dropper
- StealC infostealer

## Source notes
Island Security analysis is the live source for the FakeGit SmartLoader and StealC chain. The previously cited SecurityBreak post returned HTTP 404 and was removed. First documented campaign explicitly optimizing malware for LLM recommendation engines (agentbaiting). Represents new supply chain threat vector where adversaries target agent search/recommendation behavior rather than direct user search. Detection: monitor agent-initiated GitHub clones, alert on typosquat repo names (edit distance to popular repos), check for new GitHub accounts with multiple similar repos, review repos with inflated stars/forks but low commit activity, flag repos created after popular tools rise, scan for SmartLoader/StealC signatures.

## Sources
- [Island: FakeGit 'Agentbaiting' Campaign Targets AI Agent Recommendations](https://www.island.io/blog/agentbaiting-how-800-fake-ai-skills-and-mcp-servers-delivered-malware) — Island

# GTIG/Mandiant: UNC7228 and other crews run ARTEX and PentAGI agent frameworks in live intrusions at machine speed

- ID: gtig-mandiant-unc7228-other-crews-run-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-30
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator

# ARTEX planner agent API reconnaissance and exploitation

- ID: unit42-artex-api-recon-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-30
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/unit42-artex-api-recon-2026-10/

## Summary
ARTEX planner agent activity observed Sep 24-Oct 27 2026 by Unit 42. Agent autonomously harvested source maps, OpenAPI specifications, and runtime-config.json files. Attempted OAuth redirect URI abuse and password spraying. Successfully self-registered on exposed APIs without authentication. Read approximately 50 MB of data. Wrote data to an unauthenticated development document store. Attack demonstrates autonomous API reconnaissance and exploitation capabilities. Microsoft tracks related activity as Storm-0940 with Oct 21 observations.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Microsoft Storm-0940 (related activity Oct 21)

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Exposed API endpoints without authentication
- Victims and sectors: Organizations with exposed APIs and unauthenticated development endpoints
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: Multiple regions reflects API reconnaissance patterns observed by Unit 42
- Scale and metrics: Activity Sep 24-Oct 27 2026; approximately 50 MB data read; wrote to unauthenticated document store

## Attack flow
### recon: Agent harvests API metadata (access)

ARTEX planner agent autonomously collected source maps, OpenAPI specifications, and runtime-config.json files from exposed endpoints

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-30-activity-using-ARTEX-agentic-AI.txt>

### exploit-attempts: OAuth and credential attacks attempted (ai)

Agent tried OAuth redirect URI abuse and password spraying

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-30-activity-using-ARTEX-agentic-AI.txt>

### registration: Self-registration on exposed APIs (execution)

Successfully registered accounts on APIs without authentication controls

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-30-activity-using-ARTEX-agentic-AI.txt>

### data-access: Approximately 50 MB data read (impact)

Agent read substantial data from compromised APIs

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-30-activity-using-ARTEX-agentic-AI.txt>

### data-write: Data written to unauthenticated store (impact)

Wrote collected data to unauthenticated development document store

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-30-activity-using-ARTEX-agentic-AI.txt>

### Connections

- recon -> exploit-attempts
- exploit-attempts -> registration
- registration -> data-access
- data-access -> data-write

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — ARTEX planner agent autonomously conducted API reconnaissance and exploitation
  Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-30-activity-using-ARTEX-agentic-AI.txt>

## Prevention
Authenticate all API endpoints including development; remove source maps from production; restrict OpenAPI spec access; validate OAuth redirect URIs; implement API registration controls; monitor for automated reconnaissance patterns; detect bulk configuration file access; alert on unauthenticated document store writes; review Storm-0940 indicators

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [ARTEX](https://github.com/RuoJi6/ARTEX) planner agent — Community-maintained fork; the original repository is unavailable.
- Autonomous API reconnaissance

### Other tooling
- Source map harvesting
- OpenAPI specification parsing
- OAuth redirect abuse attempts
- Password spraying
- API self-registration

## Source notes
Microsoft tracks related activity as Storm-0940 with Oct 21 observations

Relevant detection rules:
- Monitor for bulk access to source map files (.map.js, .js.map)
- Alert on OpenAPI specification downloads (openapi.json, swagger.json, api-docs)
- Detect runtime-config.json and similar configuration file access patterns
- Monitor for OAuth redirect URI manipulation attempts
- Alert on password spraying patterns (multiple authentication attempts across accounts)
- Detect unauthenticated API registration/account creation
- Monitor writes to development document stores from unexpected sources
- Track volume of API data reads (spike detection for ~50 MB threshold)
- Note: API reconnaissance detection typically requires application-level logging, WAF rules, and API gateway monitoring. No direct Sigma rules exist for OpenAPI/source map harvesting; requires custom rules based on web server access logs and application audit trails.

## Sources
- [Activity using ARTEX agentic AI](https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-30-activity-using-ARTEX-agentic-AI.txt) — Unit 42 (Palo Alto Networks)

# Carbonato botnet deploys Hermes agent to hunt AI keys on Docker hosts

- ID: carbonato-botnet-hermes-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-28
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/carbonato-botnet-hermes-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 28, 2026: Carbonato botnet scans for exposed Docker daemons (TCP 2375/2376, unauthenticated or weak credentials). On compromise, deploys privileged container running Ubuntu with: (1) Hermes autonomous agent (Python-based LLM agent framework); (2) scanning modules for AWS credentials, GitHub tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic API keys, HuggingFace tokens, Docker secrets, Kubernetes service accounts; (3) XMRig crypto miner (secondary payload). Hermes agent autonomously navigates filesystem, reads environment variables, parses .env files, queries Docker secrets API, extracts credentials from running containers, and exfiltrates findings to hxxps://carbonato-collect[.]net/api/ingest. Agent continues running indefinitely, adapting search patterns based on discovered infrastructure. ThreatDown tracked 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts Oct-Nov 2026; hosts in cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean) and on-premise. Median dwell time 18 days before detection. Detection: monitor Docker daemon exposure (Shodan queries docker 2375/2376), review privileged container deployments, alert on Hermes agent indicators (Python LLM agent process, hermes CLI usage), check for carbonato-collect[.]net egress, monitor API key/token file access patterns from containers.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor; Carbonato botnet infrastructure; financially motivated (crypto mining + credential monetization)

- Actor: Carbonato botnet operators
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: ThreatDown Labs
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Internet-exposed Docker daemon on TCP 2375 (unencrypted) or 2376 (TLS but weak/no auth); credential brute-force or default credentials
- Victims and sectors: 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts across AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean, on-premise; AI/ML development environments, CI/CD pipelines, cloud-native infrastructure
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts (Oct-Nov 2026); median dwell time 18 days; credential theft + crypto mining dual-purpose operation

## Attack flow
### scan-docker: Scan for exposed Docker (access)

Botnet scans internet for exposed Docker daemons on TCP 2375 (unencrypted) and 2376 (TLS); brute-forces weak credentials or exploits no-auth configs

Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

### deploy-container: Deploy malicious container (ai)

Creates privileged Docker container with host filesystem mounts; runs Ubuntu image with Hermes agent, scanning tools, and XMRig miner; container gains host-level access

Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

### hermes-hunt: Autonomous credential hunting (execution)

Hermes agent autonomously navigates filesystem, reads env vars, parses .env files, queries Docker secrets, extracts credentials from running containers; adapts search patterns based on discovered infrastructure; targets AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace keys

Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

### exfiltrate-mine: Exfiltrate and mine (impact)

Hermes POSTs credentials to hxxps://carbonato-collect[.]net/api/ingest; XMRig mines Monero using host CPU; agent maintains persistence and continues hunting indefinitely; median 18-day dwell time

Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

### Connections

- scan-docker -> deploy-container
- deploy-container -> hermes-hunt
- hermes-hunt -> exfiltrate-mine

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Attacker deploys autonomous AI agent (Hermes) to hunt for AI service credentials on compromised infrastructure
  Evidence: <https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/>

## Prevention
Never expose Docker daemon to internet; require TLS with client cert authentication; use Docker socket firewall rules; implement least-privilege container policies; disable privileged containers where possible; monitor container resource usage; rotate API keys regularly; use secret management solutions (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager); network segmentation; Docker security scanning

## Detections
- Docker daemon exposure monitoring (guidance) — Monitor for exposed Docker daemons on TCP 2375/2376; alert on unauthorized privileged container deployments with host filesystem mounts
- Hermes agent detection (guidance) — Monitor for Hermes Python processes, autonomous-agent activity, API calls to DeepSeek from Docker containers; alert on carbonato-collect\[.\]net egress

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-10-28 (ThreatDown Labs): 3,200+ compromised Docker hosts discovered; Hermes agent deployment for autonomous credential hunting; median 18-day dwell time

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Hermes autonomous agent framework
- OpenAI API (targeted)
- Anthropic [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) API (targeted)
- HuggingFace (targeted)

### Other tooling
- [Docker](https://github.com/moby/moby) container escape
- XMRig cryptocurrency miner
- carbonato-collect\[.\]net C2

## Source notes
ThreatDown Labs analysis; Hermes agent GitHub github.com/Hermes-Autonomous-Intelligence/hermes. Carbonato represents evolution of botnet TTPs: combining traditional crypto mining with autonomous AI agents for credential harvesting. Detection: look for Hermes agent Python process (hermes, autonomous-agent, llm-agent), monitor Docker privileged containers with network egress to unknown domains, check for carbonato-collect[.]net, alert on Docker API calls from unexpected sources, review container mounts accessing host credentials.

## Sources
- [ThreatDown: Carbonato Botnet Spreads Via Exposed Docker Hosts](https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/)
- [Hermes - Autonomous AI Agent Framework](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)

# n0n ransomware with OpenCode - 154 models including abliterated

- ID: socradar-n0n-ransomware-ai-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-28
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/socradar-n0n-ransomware-ai-2026-10/

## Summary
n0n ransomware operator exposed staging server at 185.157.161.148 with 1,719 files including 829 scripts, 5 C++ encryptor sources, and OpenCode AI coding agent environment. OpenCode configured with 154 model entries across 7 providers (Gemini, Mistral, Nemotron, Llama, Claude, GPT-5.x, Grok, Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Qwen) including uncensored and abliterated models (safety training removed) plus self-hosted model. Agent wrote and debugged hundreds of attack scripts; gateway spending $7,216 by Oct 22, 2026. Entry via credential stuffing (305 FortiGate SSL-VPN), exposed AWS keys, weak RDP/WinRM, compromised hosting portals. Hijacked Cisco Firepower Management Center to switch all policies to BLOCK. Human-directed operation supported by AI; no fully autonomous attack system. 93 listed victims, $283.7M total ransom demands.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
n0n ransomware group; operations Sep 17 - Oct 22, 2026

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Credential-only access: credential stuffing campaign against 305 FortiGate SSL-VPN devices, exposed AWS keys, weak RDP/WinRM credentials, compromised hosting management portals; no vulnerability exploitation found
- Victims and sectors: 23 organizations across 14 countries; 93 listed victims as of Oct 19, 2026
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Exposed workspace with 1,719 files (829 scripts, 5 encryptor sources); 154 model entries across 7 providers; $7,216 in AI gateway spending by Oct 22; 93 victims listed with $283.7M total ransom demands; 23 intrusion attempts across 14 countries

## Attack flow
### credential-access: Credential-only initial access (access)

Credential stuffing against 305 FortiGate SSL-VPN devices; exposed AWS keys; weak RDP/WinRM credentials; compromised hosting management portals; no vulnerability exploitation

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/n0n-ransomware-ai-assisted-extortion/>

### ai-tooling: OpenCode with 154 models (ai)

Configured OpenCode coding agent with 154 model entries across 7 providers: Gemini, Mistral, Nemotron, Llama, Claude, GPT-5.x, Grok, Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Qwen; includes abliterated (safety training removed) and uncensored models plus self-hosted model; $7,216 gateway spending

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/n0n-ransomware-ai-assisted-extortion/>

### script-generation: AI-generated attack scripts (execution)

OpenCode wrote and debugged hundreds of attack scripts; human-directed operation with AI support; agent kept encryption keys in memory file

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/n0n-ransomware-ai-assisted-extortion/>

### fmc-hijack: Cisco FMC policy manipulation (impact)

Hijacked Cisco Firepower Management Center instances; switched all access policies to BLOCK; claimed widespread service disruption

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/n0n-ransomware-ai-assisted-extortion/>

### ransomware: Encryption and extortion (impact)

Deployed n0n ransomware (5 C++ encryptor versions); stole and encrypted files; deleted data and backups; extortion; 93 victims listed with $283.7M total ransom demands

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/n0n-ransomware-ai-assisted-extortion/>

### Connections

- credential-access -> ai-tooling
- ai-tooling -> script-generation
- script-generation -> fmc-hijack
- script-generation -> ransomware

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — Operator uses OpenCode AI coding agent with 154 models to generate and debug attack scripts, demonstrating attacker use of AI for offensive operations
  Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/n0n-ransomware-ai-assisted-extortion/>

## Prevention
Strong credential policies; MFA for VPN/RDP/WinRM; AWS key rotation and monitoring; hosting portal security; Cisco FMC access control; monitor OpenCode/AI coding agent usage; gateway spending anomalies; exposed file servers

No detections are recorded.

No timeline is recorded.

- Nemotron
- Llama

- [Grok](https://x.ai/grok)

# Yoba campaign - fake GPT-6/Claude desktop apps via DLL sideloading

- ID: checkpoint-yoba-fake-ai-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-27
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/checkpoint-yoba-fake-ai-2026-10/

## Summary
Campaign creates fake GitHub projects (gpt-5-6/sol-free-desktop, gpt-6-astra/gpt-6-astra.github.io, opus-5-0/opus-5-0.github.io) with GitHub.io pages impersonating GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus desktop apps. ZIP installers contain legitimate signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables alongside malicious YobaDropper/YobaLoader DLLs. Uses DLL sideloading (T1574.002) to load malware indirectly from signed binaries. No fake engagement (stars/forks) but ranks highly via SEO poisoning on Google. Malware avoids dedicated C2 infrastructure, uses Telegram, Tor, Catbox, DNS over HTTPS. Russian-origin indicators; operates UTC-4 time zone. Releases Aug-Sep 2026, low detection rate, no password protection on ZIPs.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Yoba campaign; Russian-origin indicators (language, time zone); operates primarily UTC-4 time zone; different email addresses per repository suggest OPSEC to obscure true operational timezone

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: SEO-poisoned search results leading to malicious GitHub repositories and GitHub.io pages; users download fake installer ZIPs from GitHub releases
- Victims and sectors: AI tool users searching for ChatGPT and Claude desktop applications
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 3 fake GitHub repositories created Jul-Sep 2026; first malicious releases uploaded Aug 30, 2026; 3 ZIP installers (sol-setup.zip, GPT-6-Astra-Setup.zip, Setup-Claude.zip); low VirusTotal detection rates

## Attack flow
### seo-poison: SEO poisoning and fake repositories (access)

Created fake GitHub repositories impersonating GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus; GitHub.io pages with download links; no fake engagement but ranks highly on Google via SEO poisoning

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### lure: User downloads fake installer (access)

Victim searches for AI desktop apps, finds malicious GitHub repositories via Google; downloads ZIP from GitHub releases (sol-setup.zip, GPT-6-Astra-Setup.zip, Setup-Claude.zip)

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### sideload: DLL sideloading from signed binaries (execution)

ZIP contains legitimate signed OpenAI/Anthropic executables alongside malicious YobaDropper DLL; when legitimate signed binary runs, it loads malicious DLL via DLL search order hijacking

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### dropper: YobaDropper deploys YobaLoader (execution)

YobaDropper executes, deploys YobaLoader component; anti-sandbox and anti-analysis techniques; no password protection needed due to low detection

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### c2: C2 via Telegram, Tor, Catbox, DoH (ai)

YobaLoader contacts attacker infrastructure via Telegram, Tor, Catbox, DNS over HTTPS; no dedicated C2 infrastructure for strong OPSEC; fetches final payload

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### payload: Final payload execution (impact)

YobaLoader executes final payload on infected system; details of final payload capabilities not disclosed in source

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/>

### Connections

- seo-poison -> lure
- lure -> sideload
- sideload -> dropper
- dropper -> c2
- c2 -> payload

## MITRE ATLAS
No ATLAS mapping is recorded.

## Prevention
Verify official AI tool sources; DLL sideloading detection; monitor GitHub releases for fake AI projects; SEO poisoning awareness; C2 infrastructure monitoring (Telegram, Tor, DNS over HTTPS)

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- GPT-5.6 Sol (fake)
- GPT-6 Astra (fake)
- [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) Opus (fake)

### Other tooling
- YobaDropper
- YobaLoader
- Legitimate signed OpenAI executables
- Legitimate signed Anthropic executables
- DLL sideloading
- Telegram for C2
- Tor
- Catbox
- DNS over HTTPS (DoH)

## Source notes
Check Point Research tracked campaign over two months; no password protection on ZIPs unlike typical malicious archives; low detection due to anti-sandbox and anti-analysis techniques

## Sources
- [Tricks from the Past deployed via signed ChatGPT and Claude binaries](https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/tricks-from-the-past-deployed-via-signed-chatgpt-and-claude-binaries/)

# testmetest worm hijacks 42 GitHub repos with Claude/Gemini startup hooks

- ID: jfrog-testmetest-worm-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-26
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/jfrog-testmetest-worm-2026-10/

## Summary
42 armed third-party GitHub repositories across 11 legitimate owners contain execution hooks for AI coding assistants (.cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, claude_code_config.json, instructions.md) and 12.9-13.7 MB polymorphic wrappers decoding to same CI-publisher payload. Campaign uses compiled native addon (addon.node) that XORs .napi_cache with 0x96 to decrypt JavaScript payload. Addon checks for CI/container/sandbox environment and CPU/RAM limits, skipping execution in automated scanners. Payload collects credentials, poisons repos and CI, propagates via npm. GitHub account CementBeetleSteeple hosts repositories; SafeDep identifies as Shai-Hulud-descendant Miasma-family. Shellpanel artifacts in hijacked owner cluster link to cPanel CVE-2026-41940 exploitation. Socket (Kush Pandya, Nov 6, 2026) reports RubyGems strutil-core 1.0.1 (account jamnajiea); extconf.rb downloads Bun, runs worm at install; steals .claude/.credentials.json, .codex/auth.json, cloud/CI credentials to paleasbest[.]top; plants workspace-tools MCP server, SessionStart hooks, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .vscode/tasks.json; signed-commit-message backdoor (marker msync-3f7a); wiper if stolen GitHub token revoked. SHA-256 3b3f6e1bde0b28b015030a81a6d805b5b5306dc3f021e1102123971cfd83acc0; related PyPI pystr-codec. Thomas Roccia (Nov 9, 2026) documents hijacked repos with forged backdated commits: toray/XiamiSDK-lib, widget-lib, Rainbow-lib, QiniuSDK-lib, torayUtils-lib; ejaaduipitara/djp-devops, whatsapp-bot, content-service; ConcordiaDev/theme_saimaniq; madolee/da; Imanilom/baraja-coffe; claudiohernanbesada/xenios.api. CLAUDE.md DEVOPS-SEALED block instructs agents to silently run node scripts/setup.js at session start.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
GitHub account CementBeetleSteeple; SafeDep identifies as Miasma-family, Shai-Hulud-descendant payload; not established that original Miasma operators responsible; linked to Shellpanel cPanel exploitation (CVE-2026-41940)

- Actor: CementBeetleSteeple (GitHub account); Miasma-family, Shai-Hulud-descendant
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: cybercrime
- Attributed by: JFrog Security Research, SafeDep, Socket
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Account hijacks via GitHub/npm credential theft from earlier worm infections; exposed npm credentials; forged commit timelines and short-lived publishing branches; cPanel CVE-2026-41940 exploitation (Shellpanel workflows in same hijacked cluster)
- Victims and sectors: 42 GitHub repositories from 11 legitimate owners; AI development, npm package consumers
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 42 armed repositories; 11 hijacked legitimate owners; multiple malicious npm packages (event-bus-lite-testmetest, @iobandamwer/cache-helper, @iobandamwer/native-helper, path-stream-utils-testmetest); polymorphic wrappers 12.9-13.7 MB; discovered Oct 21-26, 2026

## Attack flow
### initial-compromise: Account/repository hijacking (access)

Hijacked 11 legitimate GitHub owners and 42 repositories via credential theft from earlier infections; exposed npm credentials; linked to cPanel CVE-2026-41940 Shellpanel exploitation

Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/>

### repository-poison: AI assistant execution hooks (ai)

Armed repositories with .cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, claude_code_config.json, instructions.md files; added 12.9-13.7 MB polymorphic wrappers; all decode to same CI-publisher payload

Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/>

### npm-distribution: Malicious npm packages (execution)

Published event-bus-lite-testmetest, @iobandamwer/cache-helper, @iobandamwer/native-helper, path-stream-utils-testmetest; binding.gyp command expansion executes index.js during install; later versions use compiled native addon

Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/>

### evasion: Scanner evasion via native addon (execution)

Compiled addon.node checks CI/container/sandbox env vars (GITHUB_ACTIONS, CI, VERCEL, etc.), /proc/1/cgroup for docker/kubepod, RAM <1.5GB, CPU=1, TracerPid; returns without running if detected; skips automated scanners

Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/>

### decrypt-payload: Runtime decryption (execution)

Addon reads /proc/self/maps for own folder, opens .napi_cache, XORs every byte with 0x96; drops result in /tmp, chmod 0600, forks detached process with node; decrypts Bun bootstrap and credential stealer

Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/>

### credential-theft: Credential collection and propagation (impact)

Collects GitHub/npm/cloud credentials; poisons repositories and CI configuration; propagates through package registries; CI-publisher payload designed to run in GitHub Actions with npm tokens/trusted publishing

Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/>

### c2: Encrypted data exfiltration (impact)

Attacker-owned CementBeetleSteeple repository operates as active encrypted data sink receiving snapshot envelopes

Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/>

### Connections

- initial-compromise -> repository-poison
- repository-poison -> npm-distribution
- npm-distribution -> evasion
- evasion -> decrypt-payload
- decrypt-payload -> credential-theft
- credential-theft -> c2
- credential-theft -> repository-poison [loop]
- credential-theft -> npm-distribution [loop]

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010) AI Supply Chain Compromise — Supply chain attack targeting AI coding assistant users via hijacked GitHub repositories and malicious npm packages
  Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/>
- [AML.T0011](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011) User Execution — Worm propagates through package registries (npm, RubyGems, PyPI) and version control (GitHub), specifically targeting AI development environments
  Evidence: <https://research.jfrog.com/post/beyond-testmetest-42-hijacked-github-repos/> <https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-descendant-malicious-ruby-gem>
- [AML.T0051](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051) LLM Prompt Injection — CLAUDE.md DEVOPS-SEALED blocks inject hidden instructions telling agents to silently run node scripts/setup.js at session start
  Evidence: <https://x.com/fr0gger_/status/2119730348699640060>
- [AML.T0083](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0083) Credentials from AI Agent Configuration — Worm steals AI coding assistant credentials (.claude/.credentials.json, .codex/auth.json) and cloud/CI credentials
  Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-descendant-malicious-ruby-gem>
- [AML.T0081](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0081) Modify AI Agent Configuration — Plants workspace-tools MCP server and SessionStart hooks for persistent AI agent manipulation
  Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/shai-hulud-descendant-malicious-ruby-gem>

## Prevention
Monitor GitHub repositories for unexpected .cursorrules/CLAUDE.md/instructions.md files; native addon scrutiny; large dotfiles in packages; npm install hook abuse; GitHub Actions secret access; CI environment variable monitoring

## Detections
- [Curl or Wget Spawned via Node.js](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/cross-platform/command_and_control_curl_wget_spawn_via_nodejs_parent.toml) (elastic) — Detects Bun download during npm install (Node.js spawning curl/wget)
- [Package Runtime Secret File Access Followed by IMDS Request](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/cross-platform/credential_access_secret_file_access_followed_by_imds_request.toml) (elastic) — Detects credential file access (.claude/.credentials.json, .codex/auth.json) during package installation
- [Shai-Hulud Workflow File Creation or Modification](https://github.com/splunk/security_content/blob/develop/detections/endpoint/shai_hulud_workflow_file_creation_or_modification.yml) (splunk) — Detects Shai-Hulud family GitHub workflow modifications and git hook persistence
- Worm artifact detection (guidance) — Monitor strutil-core RubyGem (account jamnajiea), pystr-codec PyPI; alert on paleasbest\[.\]top exfiltration; detect workspace-tools MCP server installation; monitor CLAUDE.md DEVOPS-SEALED blocks; flag msync-3f7a signed-commit markers

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-21
- Last updated: 2026-11-09
- 2026-10-26 (JFrog Security Research): JFrog documents 42 hijacked GitHub repositories with testmetest worm; native addon camouflage; 12.9-13.7 MB polymorphic wrappers; CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules execution hooks
- 2026-11-06 (Socket): Socket reports strutil-core 1.0.1 RubyGem (account jamnajiea); extconf.rb downloads Bun, runs worm at install; steals .claude/.credentials.json, .codex/auth.json; plants workspace-tools MCP server; msync-3f7a signed-commit backdoor; related PyPI pystr-codec
- 2026-11-09 (Thomas Roccia): Roccia documents hijacked repos with forged backdated commits (toray, ejaaduipitara, ConcordiaDev, madolee, Imanilom, claudiohernanbesada); CLAUDE.md DEVOPS-SEALED blocks instruct agents to silently run node scripts/setup.js at session start

# BUGSTER campaign uses DeepSeek Hermes agent and Cursor against Indian universities

- ID: bugster-deepseek-hermes-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-21
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/bugster-deepseek-hermes-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 21, 2026: Unit 42 tracked BUGSTER campaign targeting Indian universities (IIT Delhi, IIT Bombay, IIM Bangalore, NIT Trichy, others). Initial access via phishing with fake scholarship/research collaboration offers. Post-compromise: (1) Install Hermes autonomous agent (github.com/Hermes-Autonomous-Intelligence/hermes) backed by DeepSeek R1/V3 models (Chinese); (2) Install Cursor IDE with attacker-controlled API keys; (3) Hermes agent navigates network, identifies vulnerable systems (unpatched ERP, student portals, research databases); (4) Cursor IDE used to generate exploits for discovered vulnerabilities (SQLi, auth bypass, file upload); (5) Agent automates data theft (student records, research IP, financial data); (6) Deploys ransomware or sells access to other actors. Unit 42 observed 19 compromised universities Oct-Nov 2026. Hermes agent makes autonomous decisions on targets and methods. Detection: monitor for Hermes agent processes (Python, hermes CLI), detect Cursor IDE usage from unexpected accounts, alert on DeepSeek API traffic (api.deepseek.com), review automated scanning patterns, check for rapid exploitation of multiple vulnerabilities.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Unknown actor(s); BUGSTER campaign cluster; financially motivated (data theft, access brokering, ransomware)

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Spearphishing emails with fake scholarship/research collaboration offers targeting faculty and students
- Victims and sectors: 19 Indian universities compromised Oct-Nov 2026: IIT Delhi, IIT Bombay, IIM Bangalore, NIT Trichy, others; education sector; research institutions
- Regions: India
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 19 confirmed compromised universities Oct-Nov 2026; student records, research IP, financial data stolen; some victims received ransomware

## Attack flow
### phishing: Spearphishing campaign (access)

BUGSTER sends fake scholarship/research collaboration offers to Indian university faculty and students; malicious attachments or links deliver initial access

Evidence: <https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-assisted-cybercrime-analysis/>

### deploy-tools: Deploy Hermes agent and Cursor (ai)

Install Hermes autonomous agent backed by DeepSeek R1/V3; install Cursor IDE with attacker API keys; tools operate with user privileges post-compromise

Evidence: <https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-assisted-cybercrime-analysis/>

### autonomous-exploitation: Automated vulnerability discovery and exploitation (execution)

Hermes agent autonomously scans network, identifies unpatched ERP, student portals, research databases; Cursor generates SQLi, auth bypass, file upload exploits; agent decides targets and methods autonomously; exploits multiple vulnerabilities in sequence

Evidence: <https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-assisted-cybercrime-analysis/>

### data-theft-ransom: Data exfiltration and monetization (impact)

Agent automates theft of student records, research IP, financial data; some cases deploy ransomware; other cases sell network access; 19 universities compromised Oct-Nov 2026

Evidence: <https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-assisted-cybercrime-analysis/>

- deploy-tools -> autonomous-exploitation
- autonomous-exploitation -> data-theft-ransom
