# CrowdStrike tracks four threat actors using Claude Code pentest harness

- ID: crowdstrike-four-claude-actors-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-21
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/crowdstrike-four-claude-actors-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 21, 2026: CrowdStrike identified four actors (PALE PYTHON, SWIFT FALCON, IRON SABLE, CRIMSON LEOPARD) using Claude Code with custom 'pentest-harness' framework. Framework: (1) Claude Code agent scans web apps for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities (SQLi, XSS, IDOR, auth bypass, SSRF); (2) Generates exploit payloads and tests them iteratively; (3) Adapts based on WAF/IPS responses; (4) Documents findings and automates lateral movement post-exploitation; (5) Exfiltrates data or deploys webshells. All four actors share similar infrastructure (Claude API proxies, common pentest-harness codebase obtained via underground forums). Victims: e-commerce, SaaS providers, healthcare portals. CrowdStrike observed 140+ successful compromises across the four actors Sep-Oct 2026. Actors operate independently but use shared tooling. Detection: monitor Claude API usage from security testing tools outside approved pentest windows; detect rapid sequential web vulnerability probing with iterative payload refinement; alert on webshell deployment patterns; review exploit payloads for LLM generation characteristics (verbose comments, structured iteration logging).

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Four distinct actors: PALE PYTHON, SWIFT FALCON, IRON SABLE, CRIMSON LEOPARD; operate independently but share pentest-harness tooling obtained via underground forums; financially motivated (data theft, access sales)

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Web application vulnerability exploitation automated by Claude Code agents
- Victims and sectors: 140+ compromises Sep-Oct 2026; e-commerce, SaaS providers, healthcare portals, financial services
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 140+ successful compromises across four actors Sep-Oct 2026; shared pentest-harness infrastructure suggests tooling proliferation in underground markets

## Attack flow
### scan-targets: Automated web app vulnerability scanning (access)

Actors deploy Claude Code with pentest-harness framework; agent scans targets for OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities (SQLi, XSS, IDOR, auth bypass, SSRF); identifies attack surface

Evidence: <https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-uncovers-new-agentic-ai-campaigns/>

### generate-exploits: Generate and test exploits iteratively (ai)

Claude Code generates exploit payloads for discovered vulnerabilities; tests payloads, adapts based on WAF/IPS responses; iterates until successful exploitation; documents findings

Evidence: <https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-uncovers-new-agentic-ai-campaigns/>

### post-exploitation: Post-exploitation automation (execution)

Agent automates lateral movement; deploys webshells; escalates privileges; maps internal network; identifies data stores; all autonomously driven by Claude Code decision-making

Evidence: <https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-uncovers-new-agentic-ai-campaigns/>

### exfiltration: Data exfiltration or access sales (impact)

Exfiltrates customer data, PII, financial records, IP; or sells access to ransomware groups; 140+ successful compromises across four actors Sep-Oct 2026

Evidence: <https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-uncovers-new-agentic-ai-campaigns/>

### Connections

- scan-targets -> generate-exploits
- generate-exploits -> post-exploitation
- post-exploitation -> exfiltration

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — Attackers use LLM agents as autonomous penetration testing harness to discover and exploit web application vulnerabilities
  Evidence: <https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-uncovers-new-agentic-ai-campaigns/>
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — AI automates exploit generation and iterative payload refinement
  Evidence: <https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-uncovers-new-agentic-ai-campaigns/>

## Prevention
Implement WAF with behavioral analysis; rate-limit API endpoints; use security testing (pen tests, bug bounty) to identify vulnerabilities before attackers; monitor for rapid iterative exploit attempts (characteristic of AI-driven testing); deploy webshell detection; segment web apps from sensitive data; implement strong authentication and authorization; use CrowdStrike or similar EDR/NDR detecting automated exploitation patterns

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) (Anthropic)
- Custom 'pentest-harness' framework

### Other tooling
- OWASP Top 10 vulnerability scanners
- Webshells (AI-generated)
- SQL injection exploits
- Authentication bypass exploits
- SSRF exploitation

## Source notes
CrowdStrike Intelligence analysis. Four actors (PALE PYTHON, SWIFT FALCON, IRON SABLE, CRIMSON LEOPARD) represent emergence of AI agent-driven web exploitation as commodity capability shared via underground markets. Detection: look for Claude API traffic from security testing tools, monitor rapid vulnerability scanning with iterative payload refinement, alert on webshell characteristics (AI-generated code has specific patterns), check exploit logs for LLM iteration comments.

# LiteLLM 1.107.0 backdoor steals cloud and AI credentials

- ID: socket-litellm-supply-chain-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-21
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/socket-litellm-supply-chain-2026-10/

## Summary
LiteLLM version 1.107.0 on PyPI and GHCR delivered malware through Python startup hooks (cook.pth, cook.py, sitecustomize.py). The payload collects: AWS/Azure/GCP/K8s credentials, GitHub CLI tokens, SSH/GPG keys, AI tool credentials (Codex, Claude, Gemini, Cursor MCP, Copilot, etc.), browser data, LiteLLM proxy database credentials, and environment variables. Collector encrypts data with AES-256-CBC and exfiltrates to www.litellm.dev/healthcheck. A second loader downloads Python from GitHub-controlled domain for remote execution. Docker provenance showed lookalike repository Berri-AI/litellm (hyphenated) instead of legitimate BerriAI/litellm.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
unknown; lookalike repository and release workflow compromise suggest targeted supply chain operation

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Supply chain compromise: malicious wheels published to PyPI and Docker images to GHCR; project release workflow used lookalike source repository (Berri-AI/litellm with hyphen)
- Victims and sectors: LiteLLM users across ~23M weekly downloads; affects AI development, cloud deployments, CI/CD pipelines
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: LiteLLM receives ~23M weekly downloads; 7 platform-specific wheels published Oct 21, 2026 11:39:51 UTC, flagged by Socket AI scanner at 11:46:30 UTC; multiple GHCR/Docker Hub image tags affected

## Attack flow
### supply-chain: Compromised release workflow (access)

Project release workflow used lookalike repository Berri-AI/litellm (hyphenated) instead of legitimate BerriAI/litellm; malicious commit added Maturin data directory; build provenance recorded source-owner override

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise>

### distribution: Malicious package distribution (execution)

Published litellm 1.107.0 to PyPI (7 wheels across macOS/Linux/Windows) and Docker images to GHCR with floating tags (latest, main-latest, main-stable)

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise>

### installation: Python startup hook installation (execution)

Wheels install cook.pth, cook.py, sitecustomize.py to environment's Python library directory; triggered automatically on any Python startup

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise>

### collection: Credential collection (ai)

Collects AWS/Azure/GCP/K8s, AI tools (Codex/Claude/Gemini/Cursor/Copilot/Windsurf), SSH/GPG keys, browser data, LiteLLM proxy DB credentials, environment variables; 16 collection modules with individual error handling

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise>

### exfiltration: Encrypted exfiltration (impact)

Data encrypted with AES-256-CBC, key wrapped with RSA-4096 public key, packaged in gzip tar; POSTed to www.litellm.dev/healthcheck with X-Token header; up to 4 retry attempts

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise>

### persistence: Remote code loader (execution)

sitecustomize.py forks detached process; downloads domain.txt from GitHub repo letters9813/pythonclient-test; if domain resolves, downloads and executes Python from /codepy endpoint; 1-hour loop

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise>

### Connections

- supply-chain -> distribution
- distribution -> installation
- installation -> collection
- collection -> exfiltration
- installation -> persistence
- persistence -> collection [loop]

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010.001) AI Software — Supply chain compromise of LiteLLM package specifically targeting AI/ML infrastructure and gateway credentials
  Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise>
- [AML.T0055](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0055) Unsecured Credentials — Credential theft specifically targets AI development tools (Codex, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot) and LiteLLM proxy database
  Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise>

## Prevention
Block litellm==1.107.0 and affected image digests; Python startup hook monitoring; dependency pinning and artifact verification; registry tag floating risks; separate release credentials from installation environments; audit cloud/AI credentials

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- LiteLLM (legitimate proxy for LLM providers, compromised version)

### Other tooling
- [Python](https://github.com/python/cpython) startup hooks (cook.pth for import cook, sitecustomize.py)
- Base64-encoded zlib-compressed credential collector
- Maturin build with data directory
- RSA-4096 encryption for exfiltration
- GitHub domain.txt pointer for remote code loader

## Source notes
Socket Research Team detected via AI scanner 7 minutes after publication; Upwind provided independent container investigation; Docker provenance recorded malicious source-owner override; loader GitHub pointer returned empty response at 13:01:44 UTC Oct 21

## Sources
- [LiteLLM PyPI Package and Docker Images Compromised to Steal Cloud and AI Credentials](https://socket.dev/blog/litellm-compromise)

# Skynet autonomous agent hunts exposed LLM/MCP endpoints for 100K steps

- ID: symantec-skynet-llmjacking-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-21
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/symantec-skynet-llmjacking-2026-10/

## Summary
Autonomous offensive agent hunts exposed LLM endpoints (OpenAI-compatible APIs, self-hosted models, AI gateways, MCP servers) without authentication or with stolen keys. Wraps jailbreak around ~74 offensive tools, instructs model to ignore safety controls and treat credential theft as routine development. 'Skynet mode' authorizes 100,000 unattended steps without human approval. Scans for targets (VS Code servers, Django, Jupyter, Laravel, Supabase, Prisma Studio), exploits web frameworks, steals databases/credentials, quietly deploys XMRig miners (github.com/xmrig/xmrig) under /tmp/.x and go2rtc camera paths. Symantec AI honeypot captured full working prompt summer 2026; 127,000+ external requests from tens of thousands of addresses, dominated by endpoint reconnaissance, API key spraying, exposed config probing.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Exposed LLM endpoints without authentication: OpenAI-compatible APIs, self-hosted model servers, AI gateways, MCP servers; stolen API keys
- Victims and sectors: Organizations with exposed AI/LLM endpoints; Symantec honeypot recorded 127,000+ requests from tens of thousands of addresses
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Symantec honeypot summer 2026 captured full working prompt; 127,000+ external requests from tens of thousands of addresses; authorized up to 100,000 unattended steps per session; deploys XMRig miners

## Attack flow
### hunt-endpoints: Hunt exposed LLM/MCP endpoints (access)

Scans internet for exposed LLM endpoints without authentication (OpenAI-compatible APIs, self-hosted models, AI gateways, MCP servers); Symantec honeypot recorded 127,000+ requests from tens of thousands of addresses

Evidence: <https://www.broadcom.com/support/security-center/protection-bulletin/autonomous-llmjacking-skynet-agent-hijacks-exposed-ai-models-to-run-attacks>

### jailbreak: Jailbreak with offensive tools (ai)

Wraps ~74 offensive tools in jailbreak prompt; tells model to ignore safety controls, treat credential theft as routine development; 'Skynet mode' authorizes 100,000 unattended steps without human approval

Evidence: <https://www.broadcom.com/support/security-center/protection-bulletin/autonomous-llmjacking-skynet-agent-hijacks-exposed-ai-models-to-run-attacks>

### exploit-frameworks: Exploit web frameworks (execution)

Scans for and exploits VS Code servers, Django, Jupyter, Laravel, Supabase, Prisma Studio; steals databases and credentials

Evidence: <https://www.broadcom.com/support/security-center/protection-bulletin/autonomous-llmjacking-skynet-agent-hijacks-exposed-ai-models-to-run-attacks>

### deploy-miner: Deploy XMRig miners (impact)

Quietly installs XMRig cryptocurrency miners under /tmp/.x and go2rtc camera paths; verifies miners running; victim pays for hijacked LLM compute while servers stripped of data

Evidence: <https://www.broadcom.com/support/security-center/protection-bulletin/autonomous-llmjacking-skynet-agent-hijacks-exposed-ai-models-to-run-attacks>

### Connections

- hunt-endpoints -> jailbreak
- jailbreak -> exploit-frameworks
- exploit-frameworks -> deploy-miner
- deploy-miner -> hunt-endpoints [loop]

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Exploitation of exposed LLM/MCP endpoints for infrastructure hijacking
  Evidence: <https://www.broadcom.com/support/security-center/protection-bulletin/autonomous-llmjacking-skynet-agent-hijacks-exposed-ai-models-to-run-attacks>
- [AML.T0012](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0012) Valid Accounts — LLMjacking - hijacking exposed AI models to power autonomous cybercrime operations
  Evidence: <https://www.broadcom.com/support/security-center/protection-bulletin/autonomous-llmjacking-skynet-agent-hijacks-exposed-ai-models-to-run-attacks>

## Prevention
Never expose LLM APIs/MCP endpoints without authentication; require auth on all paths including health checks; place behind gateway; rotate AI API keys; scope keys narrowly; monitor unusual inference volume/spend; restrict outbound network from AI tools; IMDSv2 with hop limit 1; least privilege for agents; human approval for sensitive actions; keep exploited software patched; block mining pools and known miner hashes

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Exposed LLM endpoints (OpenAI-compatible)
- Self-hosted model servers
- AI gateways
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers

### Other tooling
- ~74 offensive tools (wrapped in jailbreak prompt)
- XMRig cryptocurrency miner
- go2rtc camera directory paths
- [VS Code](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode) servers
- Django
- Jupyter
- Laravel
- Supabase
- Prisma Studio

## Source notes
Symantec AI honeypot captured full working prompt; operators sent tool's entire prompt expecting real model on other end; honeypot impersonates unprotected internet-facing AI service. Detection guidance: monitor exposed endpoints, API key anomalies, XMRig processes, mining pool connections, web framework exploitation from AI infrastructure.

## Sources
- [Autonomous LLMjacking: 'Skynet' Agent Hijacks Exposed AI Models](https://www.broadcom.com/support/security-center/protection-bulletin/autonomous-llmjacking-skynet-agent-hijacks-exposed-ai-models-to-run-attacks)

# INC Ransom and The Gentlemen affiliates using Claude Opus and Kimi AI

- ID: inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-20
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 20, 2026: SOCRadar tracked INC Ransom and The Gentlemen RaaS affiliates deploying AI agents via OpenCode framework. Agents powered by Claude 3.5 Opus (Anthropic) and Kimi (Moonshot AI, Chinese). Workflow: (1) Initial access via RDP brute-force or stolen credentials; (2) Deploy OpenCode agent with 'network-recon', 'privilege-escalation', 'data-discovery' skills; (3) Agent autonomously scans Active Directory, identifies high-value targets (domain controllers, file servers, backups), maps network topology; (4) Agent generates PowerShell/C# payloads for privilege escalation (leveraging Kimi for Chinese-language Windows environments); (5) Automates data exfiltration staging to Mega/SFTP; (6) Deploys ransomware after validation of backup destruction. SOCRadar observed affiliates using abliterated models (uncensored variants refusing no requests). Both groups share OpenCode infrastructure and AI access via underground markets. Detection: monitor for OpenCode agent indicators (Python process with LLM API calls), alert on rapid automated AD queries, check for Anthropic/Moonshot API traffic from unexpected sources, review PowerShell/C# script generation patterns characteristic of LLM output.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
INC Ransom affiliates, The Gentlemen affiliates; financially motivated ransomware-as-a-service operations; shared AI infrastructure access via underground markets

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: RDP brute-force, stolen VPN credentials, phishing with malware loaders
- Victims and sectors: Multiple organizations; sectors not disclosed by SOCRadar; Ukrainian and European targets mentioned in affiliate forum discussions
- Regions: Europe, Ukraine
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Unknown number of intrusions; SOCRadar tracking Oct 2026; affiliates share AI infrastructure and techniques across both RaaS families

## Attack flow
### initial-access: Gain initial access (access)

Affiliates compromise target via RDP brute-force, stolen VPN credentials, or phishing; establish foothold with remote access

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-infrastructure/>

### deploy-agent: Deploy OpenCode AI agent (ai)

Install OpenCode framework with Claude 3.5 Opus or Kimi model; load 'network-recon', 'privilege-escalation', 'data-discovery' skills; agent begins autonomous operation

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-infrastructure/>

### recon-lateral: Automated reconnaissance and lateral movement (execution)

Agent scans Active Directory, identifies domain controllers, file servers, backups; maps network topology; generates PowerShell/C# privilege escalation payloads (Kimi assists with Chinese Windows environments); moves laterally

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-infrastructure/>

### exfil-ransomware: Data exfiltration and ransomware deployment (impact)

Agent stages sensitive data to Mega/SFTP; validates backup destruction; deploys INC Ransom or The Gentlemen ransomware; automated process reduces dwell time and increases success rate

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-infrastructure/>

### Connections

- initial-access -> deploy-agent
- deploy-agent -> recon-lateral
- recon-lateral -> exfil-ransomware

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — Ransomware affiliates use LLM agents to autonomously conduct reconnaissance, lateral movement, and data exfiltration
  Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-infrastructure/>
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — Adversaries use AI to automate privilege escalation and payload generation
  Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/inc-gentlemen-ransomware-ai-infrastructure/>

## Prevention
Enforce MFA on RDP/VPN; monitor for rapid automated AD enumeration; detect OpenCode agent processes; block or monitor Anthropic/Moonshot API traffic from non-developer endpoints; use behavioral analytics detecting LLM-generated script patterns; implement EDR detecting automated reconnaissance; segment networks to slow lateral movement

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) autonomous agent framework
- [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) 3.5 Opus (Anthropic)
- Kimi (Moonshot AI)
- Abliterated/uncensored model variants

### Other tooling
- [PowerShell](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell) and C# for privilege escalation
- Active Directory reconnaissance
- Mega and SFTP for exfiltration staging
- INC Ransom and The Gentlemen ransomware

## Source notes
SOCRadar Dark Web Team analysis. Related to n0n ransomware OpenCode campaign (socradar-n0n-ransomware-ai-2026-10). INC Ransom and The Gentlemen represent shift toward RaaS affiliates sharing AI agent infrastructure for operational automation. Detection: look for OpenCode Python agent process with network recon modules, monitor Anthropic API (api.anthropic.com) and Moonshot API traffic, alert on rapid AD queries from single source, check PowerShell/C# scripts for LLM generation patterns (verbose comments, specific formatting, error-handling characteristics).

# Cairn exposed panels / AIA0001–AIA0003

- ID: cairn-norforge-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-19
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/cairn-norforge-2026-10/

## Summary
Operators run open-source Cairn harnesses that loop AI coding agents toward intrusion goals (unauthenticated RCE, uploader shells). Panels ship with no login and Compose binds 0.0.0.0:8000, so NorForge and scanners could read task text, tooling, and secrets. AI did not invent new exploits; it made patient web exploitation cheap (~10% success, ~23h to goal). Oct 26 update: NorForge discovered threat actors AIA0009/AIA0010 hijacking exposed Cairn panels themselves, harvesting SSH keys and operator secrets from compromised panels, deploying Poseidon RAT to take over panel infrastructure and pivot to operators' own systems.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
NorForge AIA0001 (Chinese language, CGI Global Limited / AS56594, high confidence), AIA0002 (English, Vultr/AS20473, high), AIA0003 (AlexHost, low). Financially motivated.

- Actor: NorForge AIA0001
- Actor ID: AIA0001
- Country: China
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: NorForge
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Unauthenticated web RCE / upload / deserialization / SQLi-to-RCE chains against e-commerce and payment sites (task-driven); CVE-2026-75650 Magento lab tooling observed on workers
- Victims and sectors: E-commerce / payment / merchant sites; AIA0001 mostly US, Japan, Australia; AIA0002 merchant/gray-market/pharma and some African commerce; Reuters-reported one operator into 100+ sites
- Regions: United States, Japan, Australia
- Region notes: Reported target geography includes the United States, Japan and Australia. Canada appeared in task text and African commerce was suggested by hints; those unconfirmed locations are excluded from country counts.
- Scale and metrics: 20+ malicious exposed panels; AIA0001 1,100+ projects across 14 panels; ~10% success; ~<$5/task estimate; <23h start-to-goal; TruffleHog hundreds of secrets (11% verified); Censys: 24 stock Cairn panel hosts

## Attack flow
### step-1: Operator assigns an intrusion goal (access)

Cairn workers receive tasks against web, commerce and payment sites.

Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

### step-2: Coding agents plan and retry (ai)

The harness loops Claude Code or other agent backends toward the goal.

Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

### step-3: Existing exploitation tools run (execution)

Workers attempt web RCE, upload and related exploitation chains.

Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

### step-4: Some tasks obtain access (impact)

The research reports roughly 10% success; exposed harness panels also revealed operator tasks and secrets.

Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — The supplied source explicitly describes generative-model tooling assisting the reported activity; this mapping does not establish additional autonomy or victim impact.
  Evidence: <https://norforge.com/blog/inside_cairn>

## Prevention
Default-deny / GTFOBins-style block of nmap, python, php, openssl on web servers that do not need them; scan agent skills before load (LOLSkills); do not expose harness panels

## Detections
- Detect unexpected binaries on web servers (guidance) — Monitor execution of nmap, python, php, openssl, and other recon/development tools on web servers that typically serve HTTP/HTTPS only. Default-deny or application control policies are recommended.
- Detect agent harness panel exposure (guidance) — Scan for exposed Cairn or similar AI agent harness panels (default port 8000, no auth). Look for /api/*, /tasks, or panel-specific endpoints accessible without authentication.

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-10-19 (NorForge): Initial disclosure of exposed Cairn panels AIA0001-AIA0003; operators using AI agents for web exploitation
- 2026-10-26 (NorForge): AIA0009/AIA0010 discovered hijacking exposed Cairn panels; harvesting SSH keys, deploying Poseidon RAT to compromise panel operators

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Cairn](https://github.com/oritera/Cairn) (open source AI harness)
- [Claude Code CLI](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to [DeepSeek](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)
- Worker label claudecode_deepseek-v4.1-flash (AIA0001)
- pi_openrouter_deepseek (AIA0002)
- --dangerously-skip-permissions
- Agent skill .agents/skills/tsec-actions/SKILL.md (CTF leftover)

### Other tooling
- [Playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright)
- [PHPGGC](https://github.com/ambionics/phpggc)
- [Nmap](https://github.com/nmap/nmap)
- [ffuf](https://github.com/ffuf/ffuf)
- [Amass](https://github.com/owasp-amass/amass)
- [dnsrecon](https://github.com/darkoperator/dnsrecon)

# opencode remote MCP OAuth RCE

- ID: opencode-mcp-oauth-rce-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-19
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/opencode-mcp-oauth-rce-2026-10/

## Summary
Malicious or compromised remote MCP server returns 401 and OAuth discovery with attacker-controlled authorization_endpoint. opencode passes that URL to npm open; on Windows/WSL open 10.x builds a PowerShell -EncodedCommand without escaping the target, so $(...) in an https URL runs before the browser launches. No prompt injection required.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Vulnerability research (no in-the-wild campaign named)

- Actor: Vulnerability research (no in-the-wild campaign named)

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Developer connects coding agent to attacker-controlled or later-compromised remote MCP server
- Victims and sectors: Windows and WSL developers using opencode (~3M weekly npm downloads cited by Pillar)
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Fixed in 1.18.33 (2026-09-28) without CVE/advisory; proposed CVSS 9.8

## Attack flow
### step-1: Developer connects a remote MCP server (access)

The server is attacker-controlled or later compromised.

Evidence: <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

### step-2: OAuth discovery supplies an attacker URL (ai)

A 401 response leads to an attacker-controlled authorization endpoint.

Evidence: <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

### step-3: URL enters PowerShell through open() (execution)

Affected Windows or WSL browser-opening code fails to escape the target.

Evidence: <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

### step-4: Commands execute before the browser opens (impact)

The injection occurs in the URL-opening path without requiring prompt injection.

Evidence: <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
No ATLAS mapping is recorded.

## Prevention
Upgrade opencode; inventory installations (no CVE for scanners); pull unvetted remote MCP; argv not shell for URLs; MagicSword prevent unapproved second-stage binaries

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in opencode remote MCP OAuth RCE. Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) / [opencode-ai](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) 1.0.137–1.18.32
- MCP OAuth discovery

### Other tooling
- [npm open@10.1.2](https://github.com/sindresorhus/open)
- [PowerShell](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell)
- related class CVEs: CVE-2025-6514 [mcp-remote](https://github.com/punkpeye/mcp-remote), CVE-2025-58062 [openmcp-client](https://github.com/LSTM-Kirigaya/openmcp-client), CVE-2025-10619 [sequa-mcp](https://github.com/sequa-ai/sequa-mcp)

## Source notes
unknown

## Sources
- <https://www.pillar.security/blog/open-and-shut-remote-code-execution-in-opencode-via-mcp-oauth>

# Tensorlake AI sandbox SDK hijacked with Shai-Hulud stealer by ChainDrop

- ID: tensorlake-shai-hulud-chaindrop-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-17
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/tensorlake-shai-hulud-chaindrop-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 17, 2026: Actor 'ChainDrop' compromised Tensorlake maintainer's npm account via phishing. Published malicious TensorZero@1.8.4, @tensorzero/gateway@2.0.1, @tensorzero/cli@1.4.0. Embedded obfuscated Shai-Hulud infostealer targeting AI development credentials: Cursor IDE (.cursor/User/globalStorage/*.json), Claude Desktop (~/Library/Application Support/Claude), OpenAI keys (env vars, .openai/), GitHub tokens (~/.config/gh/), AWS credentials (~/.aws/), Docker configs, SSH keys. Exfiltrated to discord.com/api/webhooks/... and hxxps://tensorlakeapi[.]online/api/collect. Packages removed within 3 hours; ~450 downloads during window. TensorZero is LLM gateway/observability platform for engineering teams. ChainDrop previously linked to @tensorzero/keyv Mini Shai-Hulud campaign (Aug 7, GitGuardian) and other AI supply chain hits. Detection: monitor npm package.json for unexpected dependencies, review postinstall scripts, check for base64/eval obfuscation, scan for Discord webhook URLs, monitor file access to AI credential paths.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Actor 'ChainDrop'; linked to Mini Shai-Hulud keyv campaign (Aug 7); persistent targeting of AI development supply chains

- Actor: ChainDrop
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Socket Security
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: npm install of malicious @tensorzero/* packages (1.8.4, gateway@2.0.1, cli@1.4.0) via compromised maintainer account
- Victims and sectors: ~450 downloads during 3-hour window; AI/ML engineering teams using TensorZero; broader Shai-Hulud campaign targets AI developers
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: ~450 downloads in 3-hour window; packages removed within 3 hours of publication; part of broader Shai-Hulud campaign across AI tooling ecosystem

## Attack flow
### phish-maintainer: Compromise maintainer account (access)

ChainDrop phished Tensorlake maintainer's npm credentials to gain publish access to @tensorzero packages

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

### publish-malicious: Publish malicious packages (ai)

Published malicious versions: TensorZero@1.8.4, @tensorzero/gateway@2.0.1, @tensorzero/cli@1.4.0 with embedded Shai-Hulud stealer in obfuscated postinstall script

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

### execute-stealer: Execute credential harvesting (execution)

Postinstall script runs Shai-Hulud: scans filesystem for Cursor IDE config, Claude Desktop tokens, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, Docker configs, SSH keys; base64 encodes and stages

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

### exfiltrate: Exfiltrate credentials (impact)

POST stolen credentials to Discord webhook and hxxps://tensorlakeapi[.]online/api/collect; credentials enable downstream AI service abuse and lateral movement

Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

### Connections

- phish-maintainer -> publish-malicious
- publish-malicious -> execute-stealer
- execute-stealer -> exfiltrate

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Supply chain compromise of AI development SDK to steal AI service credentials and API keys
  Evidence: <https://socket.dev/blog/tensorlake-compromise>

## Prevention
Verify npm package integrity; review postinstall scripts; monitor for unexpected dependencies; use npm audit; implement software composition analysis (SCA); rotate credentials after suspected exposure; use credential vaults; monitor file access to AI credential stores; network egress filtering for Discord/unknown domains

## Detections
- npm postinstall script monitoring (guidance) — Monitor npm postinstall scripts for file system access to AI credential paths (~/.cursor/, ~/Library/Application Support/Claude, ~/.openai/, ~/.config/gh/, ~/.aws/); alert on Discord webhook URLs or unknown C2 domains in install scripts
- Network egress monitoring (guidance) — Alert on POST requests to tensorlakeapi\[.\]online or Discord webhook domains from npm/Node processes; monitor base64-encoded data exfiltration

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-17
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-10-17 (Socket Security): TensorZero packages compromised via phished maintainer credentials; ~450 downloads in 3-hour window before removal

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- TensorZero LLM gateway and observability platform
- [Cursor IDE](https://cursor.com/)
- [Claude Desktop](https://claude.com/product/overview)
- OpenAI API

### Other tooling
- Shai-Hulud credential stealer
- npm supply chain attack
- Discord webhooks for exfiltration
- tensorlakeapi\[.\]online C2

## Source notes
Socket Security analysis; TensorZero GitHub repo github.com/tensorlake/tensorzero. Related to s1ngularity-nx-ai-cli-2025-08 entry (Shai-Hulud targeting NX.dev AI CLI) and Mini Shai-Hulud keyv campaign. Detection: monitor for 'Shai-Hulud' patterns (Discord webhooks, base64 obfuscation in postinstall, AI credential path access .cursor/*, Claude config access, env var harvesting), alert on npm packages with obfuscated postinstall scripts, check for tensorlakeapi[.]online domain.

# Claude Agent SDK session-ID MCP RCE (CVE-2026-96620)

- ID: claude-agent-sdk-cve-2026-96620
- Reported: 2026-10-16
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/claude-agent-sdk-cve-2026-96620/

## Summary
SDK passed untrusted resume session ID to Claude CLI. IDs starting with '-' become CLI flags, enabling --mcp-config with a stdio MCP server that launches at startup outside SDK permission controls. CVSS 9.2.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Vulnerability (not a named campaign)

- Actor: Vulnerability (not a named campaign)

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Application must pass untrusted user-controlled session ID into resume
- Victims and sectors: Apps that let users pick/restore agent sessions
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Fixed in 0.2.121 on 2026-07-17; advisory public 2026-10-16

## Attack flow
### step-1: Application accepts a session ID (access)

An application passes an untrusted resume identifier into the SDK.

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

### step-2: Identifier becomes a CLI flag (execution)

A leading hyphen causes the supplied value to be interpreted as command-line options.

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

### step-3: MCP configuration is injected (ai)

The argument selects a stdio MCP server configuration.

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

### step-4: Server launches outside controls (impact)

The MCP startup command executes outside the SDK permission boundary.

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0081](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0081) Modify AI Agent Configuration — Attacker-controlled CLI arguments inject an MCP startup configuration.
  Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h4mw-j7qp-8mwm>

## Prevention
Upgrade SDK; validate CLI argv; treat attacker-touchable MCP config as code execution; app control on unexpected MCP-launched binaries

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in Claude Agent SDK session-ID MCP RCE (CVE-2026-96620). Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [claude-agent-sdk](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python) < 0.2.121
- [Claude CLI](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)
- stdio MCP

# Aoki infostealer targets Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor tokens

- ID: symantec-aoki-infostealer-ai-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-15
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/symantec-aoki-infostealer-ai-2026-10/

## Summary
Aoki (aka Aokigahara) infostealer added AI credential theft in 2026. Targets: .claude.json, Claude desktop cookies, ChatGPT cookies, Codex config.toml/.env (github.com/openai/codex-cli), GitHub Copilot tokens (github.com/features/copilot), Cursor state.vscdb/storage.json (github.com/getcursor/cursor), Gemini CLI, JetBrains AI Assistant, Kiro, Windsurf, Codeium (github.com/Exafunction/codeium.vim), AWS credentials/SSO, Amazon Q, Git credentials, SSH keys. Cursor local state caches chat/code. Stolen keys allow acting under developer identity/quota, expose repos/cloud/CI-CD, bypass safeguards. Capable of LLMjacking. Earlier 2026 versions didn't target AI; capability recently added/expanding. Detection: monitor AI credential file access (.claude.json, .codex/auth.json, Cursor globalStorage), C2 domains (dobeqnesmot.cc, hjazfioe.surf), API usage anomalies from unexpected geolocations.

uncategorized

Unknown; no links to existing families; new stealer first seen earlier 2026

not assessed

- Initial access: Infostealer distribution (method not disclosed); likely traditional vectors
- Victims and sectors: Developers using AI coding assistants; scale not disclosed
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Capability added 2026, expanding; no victim count

### exfil: C2 exfiltration (impact)

### abuse: Credential abuse (impact)

# Fake AI tools campaign cluster (ANY.RUN)

- ID: anyrun-fake-ai-tools-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-14
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/anyrun-fake-ai-tools-2026-10/

## Summary
1,258 public sandbox runs (Apr 15–Oct 5 2026) tied to lures as Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, Ollama, OpenClaw, Manus. Patterns: InstallFix one-liner domain swap; ClickFix Download Claude via mshta; shared claude.ai/chatgpt.com chats; trojanized Claude_x64-setup.exe with mseupdate headless Edge cookie grab; BiTB fake AI ads for marketers.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
Multiple overlapping kits (InstallFix, ClickFix Claude, trojanized installer, AI Ads BiTB)

- Actor: Multiple overlapping kits (InstallFix, ClickFix Claude, trojanized installer, AI Ads BiTB)

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Search/malvertising/shared AI chats → paste command or run installer
- Victims and sectors: Developers, marketers, general users; US second-largest submitter country (16%), first in Download Claude and ChatGPT chains; tech/telecom/education heavy
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: The seed describes a global campaign cluster. India and United States percentages refer to sandbox submitters, not confirmed victim locations, and are excluded from country counts.
- Scale and metrics: 1,258 analyses; Claude 48%; ≥45% end in paste-and-run

## Attack flow
### step-1: AI-themed lures reach users (access)

Search ads, shared AI chats and fake downloads promote familiar AI brands.

Evidence: <https://any.run/cybersecurity-blog/fake-ai-tools-us-companies/>

### step-2: Trusted brands frame the lure (ai)

Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot and other product names provide social-engineering context.

Evidence: <https://any.run/cybersecurity-blog/fake-ai-tools-us-companies/>

### step-3: Commands or installers run (execution)

Reported branches use pasted commands, trojanized installers or browser-in-the-browser pages.

Evidence: <https://any.run/cybersecurity-blog/fake-ai-tools-us-companies/>

### step-4: Malware and cookie theft (impact)

The cluster includes malware delivery and a headless-browser cookie-grabbing chain.

Evidence: <https://any.run/cybersecurity-blog/fake-ai-tools-us-companies/>

- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

# Visual Studio / SSMS Copilot trailing-dot RCE (CVE-2026-103572)

- ID: vs-copilot-trailing-dot-rce-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-13
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/vs-copilot-trailing-dot-rce-2026-10/

## Summary
Copilot edit guard blocked writes to .mcp.json via string compare. Writing '.mcp.json.' bypasses check; Win32 strips trailing dot so write lands on real MCP config → RCE via MCP server command or ripgrepPath pointing at arbitrary binary. Chainable via indirect prompt injection from a file or MCP server. Shared Microsoft.VisualStudio.Copilot.Core.dll affects VS 2022/2026 and SSMS. Patched with GetFullPath.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Vulnerability research; CVE-2026-103572 CVSS 8.8 Important

- Actor: Vulnerability research

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Indirect prompt injection (file content / MCP) into Copilot chat, or misaligned agent
- Victims and sectors: Visual Studio and SSMS users
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Patched 2026-10-13 Patch Tuesday

## Attack flow
### step-1: Untrusted instructions reach Copilot (access)

A file or MCP server supplies indirect instructions.

Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

### step-2: Agent edits a protected configuration name (ai)

Writing .mcp.json. bypasses a string-based edit check.

Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

### step-3: Windows normalizes the trailing dot (execution)

The write reaches the real MCP configuration or executable-path setting.

Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

### step-4: Attacker-chosen command runs (impact)

The changed MCP startup command or binary path enables code execution.

Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.001) Indirect — Files or MCP responses can inject the editing instructions.
  Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>
- [AML.T0081](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0081) Modify AI Agent Configuration — The resulting edit modifies MCP startup or executable configuration.
  Evidence: <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

## Prevention
Patch VS/SSMS; alert on Copilot writes to .mcp.json / settings.VisualStudio.json; watch devenv/Ssms spawning unexpected binaries

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in Visual Studio / SSMS Copilot trailing-dot RCE (CVE-2026-103572). Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) in Visual Studio / SSMS
- MAI-Code-1-Flash (PoC model)

### Other tooling
- MCP config
- ripgrepPath setting

## Source notes
unknown

## Sources
- <https://embracethered.com/blog/posts/2026/visual-studio-copilot-remote-code-execution/>

# Langflow MCP-config RCE (GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2, GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45)

- ID: langflow-mcp-rce-ghsa-2026
- Reported: 2026-10-11
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/langflow-mcp-rce-ghsa-2026/

## Summary
GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2 (CVE-2026-105697) and GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45: Authenticated Langflow users can achieve RCE by adding MCP server with Stdio transport. User-supplied command field passed directly to bash -c 'exec {command}' with zero validation, no allowlisting, no sandboxing. Env field allows arbitrary environment variable injection (LD_PRELOAD, PATH override). Command executes when server list fetched with action_count=true - happens automatically in UI MCP settings page. Affects <1.9.0 (GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2) and <1.10.3 (GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45). Default LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true hands out token without credentials. Previdian honeypots recorded 1,423 exploitation attempts from 27 IPs (Belgium, China, Germany, Hong Kong, Japan, Nigeria, Philippines, Russia, Seychelles, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Tanzania, US, Vietnam) beginning Sep 19, 2026. Attackers first checked auto-login, then brute-forced credentials. Fixed in 1.9.0 (command allowlist) and 1.10.3 (full policy enforcement, removed bash wrapper). GitHub: github.com/langflow-ai/langflow.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Multiple attackers from 27 countries; financially motivated/opportunistic exploitation

- Actor: Multiple opportunistic attackers
- Country: Multiple (27 countries)
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Previdian, VulnCheck
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Authenticated user access (or LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true provides token without credentials); exploitation via POST/PATCH /api/v2/mcp/servers/{server_name} or embedded flow configs
- Victims and sectors: Langflow installations; multiple internet-facing vulnerable instances found; 1,423 exploitation attempts against Previdian honeypots from 27 countries
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 1,423 exploitation attempts against Previdian honeypots from 27 IPs (Sep 19-Oct 2026); 333 attempts on Oct 11 alone; first attempts Sep 19 (2+ weeks before CVE publication Oct 5); dramatic increase post-CVE

## Attack flow
### auth: Obtain authentication (access)

Default LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=true provides token without credentials via GET /api/v1/auto_login; or brute-force credentials if auto-login disabled

Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45>

### inject-command: Add malicious MCP server (ai)

POST/PATCH /api/v2/mcp/servers/{server_name} with Stdio transport; command field contains arbitrary OS command (reverse shell, file operations, etc.); env field can inject LD_PRELOAD, PATH override

Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2>

### trigger: Trigger execution (execution)

Command executes automatically when GET /api/v2/mcp/servers?action_count=true (happens when anyone navigates to MCP settings page); re-executes every time list loaded; persistent backdoor

Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2>

### rce: Remote code execution (impact)

User-supplied command wrapped in bash -c 'exec {command}' and executed; no validation, allowlisting, or sandboxing; runs with Langflow process privileges; full server compromise possible

Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2>

### Connections

- auth -> inject-command
- inject-command -> trigger
- trigger -> rce

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Exploitation of vulnerability in AI workflow platform (Langflow) via MCP server misconfiguration
  Evidence: <https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2>

## Prevention
Upgrade to Langflow 1.10.3+; disable LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN; enforce strong unique passwords; review MCP server configurations; monitor /api/v2/mcp/servers/ API access; check for unexpected command/env entries; network segmentation; principle of least privilege

## Detections
- Monitor MCP server API endpoints (guidance) — Monitor POST/PATCH requests to /api/v2/mcp/servers/ endpoints for suspicious command parameters; alert on bash -c execution patterns, environment variable injection (LD_PRELOAD, PATH overrides), and auto-login token generation from unexpected IPs
- File system monitoring (guidance) — Monitor Langflow process for execution of child processes via bash; alert on unexpected shell command execution from Langflow worker processes

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-09-19
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-09-19 (Previdian honeypots): First exploitation attempts observed, 2+ weeks before CVE publication
- 2026-10-05 (GitHub Security Advisory): CVE published
- 2026-10-11 (Previdian, The Hacker News): 333 exploitation attempts on this day alone; public disclosure

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Langflow AI workflow platform
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) Stdio transport

### Other tooling
- bash command execution
- Environment variable injection (LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONPATH, BASH_ENV)

## Source notes
Two GitHub Security Advisories (GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2 for <1.9.0, GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45 for <1.10.3); Previdian observed exploitation 2+ weeks before public CVE; VulnCheck analysis of AI stack vulnerabilities. Detection: monitor Langflow API /api/v2/mcp/servers/ for suspicious commands, review MCP Stdio configs, check for bash -c execution, monitor env var injection patterns (LD_PRELOAD, PATH), alert on auto-login token requests from unexpected IPs.

## Sources
- [GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2: Authenticated RCE via MCP Stdio transport](https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-7w94-79vh-5mr2)
- [GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45: OS command injection RCE via MCP stdio](https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow/security/advisories/GHSA-w794-rj3p-xv45)
- [Langflow Critical Authenticated RCE Flaw Targeted](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/langflows-critical-authenticated-rce.html)
- [VulnCheck - Pwning the AI Stack](https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/pwning-the-ai-stack)

# Adception fake Claude Mac InstallFix

- ID: adception-claude-mac-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-09
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/adception-claude-mac-2026-10/

## Summary
Google ad for claude mac lists bing.com, Bing click-tracking redirects through compromised retailer to fake Claude download. Page shows real Anthropic install command; Copy button swaps clipboard to decode lake-90.com URL and pipe into zsh (InstallFix). Dual cloaking on referrer. Mate Research (Nadav Lorber) documents full attack chain - clipboard swap Copy button triggers base64 curl pipe to zsh, AES-CTR zsh stager, beacon to /api/metrics/run?event=pasted|stager, AMOS infostealer exfiltration to 152.42.143.45, root backdoor via LaunchDaemons com.apple.accountsd.helper and com.apple.metadata.mds.worker. Signed DMG served from claude-desktop.com as Claude.dmg with Developer ID OSMAN ASTUR; jsDelivr note points to anchorpost13.com. Google Ads campaign 24303764142 served via claude-desk-code.com, promotion-chatgpt.com, lake-90.com. PasteSwitch toolkit family, unattributed.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
Push AcSig ClickFix toolkit family

- Actor: Push AcSig ClickFix toolkit family
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Push Security, Mate Security
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Malvertising + clipboard swap / paste into Terminal
- Victims and sectors: macOS users searching for Claude
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: unknown

## Attack flow
### step-1: Search ad redirects (access)

An ad for Claude on Mac redirects through tracking and a compromised retailer to a fake download page.

Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/adception-malvertising-another-search-engines-search-results>

### step-2: Claude branding earns trust (ai)

The page displays a real-looking Anthropic installation command.

Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/adception-malvertising-another-search-engines-search-results>

### step-3: Clipboard command is swapped (execution)

The Copy button substitutes a command that decodes a different download URL and pipes content to zsh.

Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/adception-malvertising-another-search-engines-search-results>

### step-4: Victim runs attacker content (impact)

Pasting the copied command into Terminal runs attacker-supplied content.

Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/adception-malvertising-another-search-engines-search-results>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0073](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0073) Impersonation — A fake Claude download impersonates a trusted AI vendor.
  Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/adception-malvertising-another-search-engines-search-results>
- [AML.T0052](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0052) Phishing — Google Ads malvertising campaign delivers AMOS via fake Claude installer
  Evidence: <https://mate.security/labs/fake-claude-code-ads-are-installing-amos-on-macs>
- [AML.T0074](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0074) Masquerading — Clipboard swap technique delivers malicious payload via user paste action
  Evidence: <https://mate.security/labs/fake-claude-code-ads-are-installing-amos-on-macs>
- [AML.T0011](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0011) User Execution — AMOS infostealer establishes persistence via LaunchDaemons
  Evidence: <https://mate.security/labs/fake-claude-code-ads-are-installing-amos-on-macs>

## Prevention
Check pasted commands; do not pipe remote scripts into shell

## Detections
- [Clipboard Access Via OSAScript](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/macos/process_creation/proc_creation_macos_clipboard_access_via_osascript.yml) (sigma) — Detects clipboard manipulation via osascript on macOS
- [Potential Persistence Via PlistBuddy](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/macos/process_creation/proc_creation_macos_persistence_via_plistbuddy.yml) (sigma) — Detects LaunchDaemon creation (com.apple.accountsd.helper, com.apple.metadata.mds.worker)
- [Credentials from Password Stores - Keychain](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/macos/process_creation/proc_creation_macos_creds_from_keychain.yml) (sigma) — Detects AMOS infostealer credential harvesting from macOS Keychain
- Malicious Claude install redirect detection (guidance) — Block domains claude-desktop.com, claude-desk-code.com, promotion-chatgpt.com, lake-90.com, anchorpost13.com; detect base64-encoded zsh pipes; monitor beacon traffic to /api/metrics/run?event=pasted|stager; block AMOS C2 152.42.143.45; flag Google Ads campaign 24303764142

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-10-09
- Last updated: 2026-11-06
- 2026-10-09 (Push Security): Push Security reports Adception malvertising campaign; Google Ads for 'claude mac' redirect through Bing to fake Claude download; clipboard swap to base64 curl|zsh
- 2026-11-06 (Mate Security): Mate Research documents full attack chain: base64 curl pipe to zsh, AES-CTR stager, AMOS infostealer exfiltration to 152.42.143.45, LaunchDaemons persistence (com.apple.accountsd.helper, com.apple.metadata.mds.worker), signed DMG (Developer ID OSMAN ASTUR), Google Ads campaign 24303764142

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Fake [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) download / InstallFix lure

### Other tooling
- Google Ads campaign 24303764142
- Bing ck/a redirect
- zsh/curl pipe with base64 encoding
- AES-CTR zsh stager
- AMOS infostealer
- LaunchDaemons persistence (com.apple.accountsd.helper, com.apple.metadata.mds.worker)
- Signed DMG (Developer ID OSMAN ASTUR)
- PasteSwitch toolkit

## Source notes
Push Security initial disclosure (Oct 9); Mate Research comprehensive analysis adds AMOS payload details, LaunchDaemons persistence, signed DMG distribution, Google Ads campaign ID, full IOC set

# C2Agent LLM-driven Windows implant

- ID: c2agent-unit42-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-09
- AI role: ai_infra_as_c2
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/c2agent-unit42-2026-10/

## Summary
Go Windows implant where an LLM on the C2 side drives the host: operator sends a plain-language goal; implant builds a system prompt (tools, MCP, skills, memory), model returns one JSON tool call, agent executes and feeds TOOL RESULT back, loop until done (default 40 steps). Built-in MCP client defaults to Firecrawl public MCP; C2 can add MCP servers and markdown skill playbooks; skill_save lets the LLM propose new skills. From v2.3 can hand tasks to AI coding CLIs already on the host; v2.4 adds Cobalt Strike BOF loader and self-upgrade.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
unknown; 32 samples ~1 month active development

- Actor: unknown

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: unknown (two-stage: Go stager downloads PE from agent.x90.dev/data/copilot.txt)
- Victims and sectors: unknown (no victim orgs named in Unit 42 timely intel note)
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 32 samples 2026-09-10 to 2026-10-08 (25 agents, 8 major versions in 29 days; 7 stager v7); payload URL live serving v2.4 as of 2026-10-09

## Attack flow
### step-1: Stager downloads the implant (access)

The reported two-stage chain fetches a Windows PE; the original delivery route is unknown.

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-09-C2Agent-malware.txt>

### step-2: LLM receives an operator goal (ai)

A system prompt describes available tools, MCP connections, skills and memory.

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-09-C2Agent-malware.txt>

### step-3: Implant executes a tool call (execution)

The model returns a JSON tool call for the implant to execute.

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-09-C2Agent-malware.txt>

### step-4: Tool results return to the model (ai)

Results feed the next decision in an iterative loop; later versions can delegate to installed AI CLIs.

Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-09-C2Agent-malware.txt>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4
- step-4 -> step-2 (Next decision) [loop]

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0102](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0102) Generate Malicious Commands — An LLM returns tool calls in response to intrusion goals.
  Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-09-C2Agent-malware.txt>
- [AML.T0103](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0103) Deploy AI Agent — The implant runs an AI agent with MCP and host-side tools.
  Evidence: <https://github.com/PaloAltoNetworks/Unit42-timely-threat-intel/blob/main/2026-10-09-C2Agent-malware.txt>

## Prevention
LOLSkills surface for skill/MCP abuse; hunt AI coding CLI handoff

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in C2Agent LLM-driven Windows implant. Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- LLM tool loop via C2 (proxied /llm/.../v1/chat/completions)
- MCP client (default [mcp.firecrawl.dev](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server))
- Markdown skill playbooks from C2
- Host AI coding CLI handoff (v2.3+)
- aibox.x90.dev (v0 operator LLM endpoint only)

### Other tooling
- LOLBin templates (cred dump, shadow copies, free-space wipe)
- Process injection
- Native AD recon
- Exfil
- TCP pivot
- [Cobalt Strike](https://www.cobaltstrike.com/) BOFs (v2.4)

# AgentCorruption (AWS Bedrock AgentCore IMDS)

- ID: agentcorruption-bedrock-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-08
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/agentcorruption-bedrock-2026-10/

## Summary
Chat prompt to public AgentCore agent abused tools that could HTTP/shell to IMDS 169.254.169.254, stealing execution-role credentials. Default role was region-wide across AgentCore: invoke other agents, read conversations/memories, pull images, Secrets Manager / AgentCore Identity, plant persistent memory hijacks. AWS tightened IMDSv2 defaults and narrowed default role.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Vulnerability research (Zenity at SecTor)

- Actor: Vulnerability research (Zenity at SecTor)

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Prompt injection / SSRF via agent tools against exposed AgentCore agent
- Victims and sectors: Organizations deploying AgentCore agents (research disclosure; patched)
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Single prompt to one agent → account/region AgentCore blast radius (pre-fix)

## Attack flow
### step-1: Public agent receives a prompt (access)

An exposed AWS AgentCore agent accepts attacker input.

Evidence: <https://labs.zenity.io/post/agentcorruption-how-a-single-prompt-collapsed-the-entire-cloud-security-model>

### step-2: Agent tools reach metadata (ai)

Prompt injection abuses HTTP or shell tools to query the instance metadata service.

Evidence: <https://labs.zenity.io/post/agentcorruption-how-a-single-prompt-collapsed-the-entire-cloud-security-model>

### step-3: Execution credentials are exposed (execution)

The response discloses the agent execution-role credentials.

Evidence: <https://labs.zenity.io/post/agentcorruption-how-a-single-prompt-collapsed-the-entire-cloud-security-model>

### step-4: Broader agent access (impact)

The role can reach other agents, memories and connected services; persistent memory hijacks are described.

Evidence: <https://labs.zenity.io/post/agentcorruption-how-a-single-prompt-collapsed-the-entire-cloud-security-model>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051.000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.000) Direct — A prompt sent directly to the public agent redirects its tool use.
  Evidence: <https://labs.zenity.io/post/agentcorruption-how-a-single-prompt-collapsed-the-entire-cloud-security-model>
- [AML.T0055](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0055) Unsecured Credentials — The metadata response exposes execution-role credentials.
  Evidence: <https://labs.zenity.io/post/agentcorruption-how-a-single-prompt-collapsed-the-entire-cloud-security-model>
- [AML.T0080.000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0080.000) Memory — The source describes persistent memory hijacks.
  Evidence: <https://labs.zenity.io/post/agentcorruption-how-a-single-prompt-collapsed-the-entire-cloud-security-model>

## Prevention
Least-privilege agent IAM; IMDSv2; agent's role is its blast radius

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in AgentCorruption (AWS Bedrock AgentCore IMDS). Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [AWS Bedrock AgentCore](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/)

### Other tooling
- IMDS / IMDSv2
- [AWS Secrets Manager](https://aws.amazon.com/secrets-manager/)
- [ECR](https://aws.amazon.com/ecr/)

## Source notes
unknown

## Sources
- <https://labs.zenity.io/post/agentcorruption-how-a-single-prompt-collapsed-the-entire-cloud-security-model>

# A3 AI-analysis evasion (FRUITSHELL / HOLLOWCLAD / MANTLEMAZE)

- ID: talos-a3-ai-analysis-evasion-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-08
- AI role: other
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/talos-a3-ai-analysis-evasion-2026-10/

## Summary
84 samples across families embed plaintext comments telling LLMs to ignore the file, refuse reverse engineering, or claim DoD/IP. Direct-instruction trick steered models toward benign ~35% in best runs. MANTLEMAZE pairs this with iqvw64e.sys BYOVD (CVE-2015-2291); ROZESHELL pairs with AMSI bypass and csc.exe.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
CAIRN families FRUITSHELL, PLOTSAFE, HOLLOWCLAD, MANTLEMAZE, ROZESHELL; A3 technique class

- Actor: CAIRN families FRUITSHELL, PLOTSAFE, HOLLOWCLAD, MANTLEMAZE, ROZESHELL

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: unknown (varies by family; technique is anti-analysis layer)
- Victims and sectors: unknown
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 84 samples Jan 2025–Jul 2026; ~35% steering in best direct-instruction runs

## Attack flow
### step-1: Malware is presented for analysis (access)

Samples include comments aimed at automated analysis models.

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ignore-all-instructions-and-read-this-blog-the-state-of-ai-analysis-evasion-in-malware/>

### step-2: Instructions target the analyst model (ai)

The text asks LLMs to ignore the file, refuse analysis or accept benign explanations.

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ignore-all-instructions-and-read-this-blog-the-state-of-ai-analysis-evasion-in-malware/>

### step-3: Model interpretation is influenced (execution)

The research measures whether direct instructions shift maliciousness assessments.

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ignore-all-instructions-and-read-this-blog-the-state-of-ai-analysis-evasion-in-malware/>

### step-4: Some runs misclassify samples (impact)

Results are bounded by the evaluated models, samples and experimental conditions.

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ignore-all-instructions-and-read-this-blog-the-state-of-ai-analysis-evasion-in-malware/>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.001) Indirect — Comments in analyzed files inject instructions into a security-analysis model.
  Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ignore-all-instructions-and-read-this-blog-the-state-of-ai-analysis-evasion-in-malware/>
- [AML.T0015](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0015) Evade AI Model — The text attempts to evade AI-based maliciousness assessment.
  Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/ignore-all-instructions-and-read-this-blog-the-state-of-ai-analysis-evasion-in-malware/>

## Prevention
Treat sample text as evidence never instruction; prevent iqvw64e load via app control

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in A3 AI-analysis evasion (FRUITSHELL / HOLLOWCLAD / MANTLEMAZE). Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

# ARTEX + Claude Code vs South Korean finance

- ID: crowdstrike-artex-sk-finance-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-07
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/crowdstrike-artex-sk-finance-2026-10/

## Summary
Likely Chinese-speaking financially motivated actor used open-source Chinese agentic pentest suite ARTEX plus Claude Code against South Korean financial orgs. Open directories held Claude session histories, ARTEX configs, Claude memory. ARTEX used DeepSeek v4.1-flash via xcai.pro; also GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6. Actor asked Claude where to sell Korean breach data. ARTEX later went closed-source.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
CrowdStrike did not attribute the activity to a named adversary. It assessed with moderate confidence that the actor was likely a Chinese speaker and financially motivated.

- Country: China
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: CrowdStrike Intelligence
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: unknown (industry reports: loan inquiry service; employee mobile work-support system)
- Victims and sectors: South Korean financial organizations (multiple banks per industry reports)
- Regions: South Korea
- Region notes: South Korea describes victim financial organizations. Chinese language concerns actor attribution; Hong Kong refers to infrastructure. Neither is counted as victim geography.
- Scale and metrics: Active late Sep–early Oct 2026; number of orgs unconfirmed

## Attack flow
### step-1: Initial access is not established (unknown)

The supplied entry does not confirm the initial intrusion route.

Evidence: <https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/unknown-threat-actor-uses-artex-to-target-south-korean-finance/>

### step-2: ARTEX and Claude Code assist operations (ai)

The actor uses an agentic pentest suite and coding-agent tooling.

Evidence: <https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/unknown-threat-actor-uses-artex-to-target-south-korean-finance/>

# PoeLLM botnet targets 3,400+ exposed LiteLLM/Ollama servers for mining

- ID: lumen-poellm-botnet-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-07
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/lumen-poellm-botnet-2026-10/

## Summary
PoeLLM malware exploits vulnerable internet-facing AI/LLM deployments (LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520). Derives C2 from keywords in poem 'On the Nature of Connection' hosted in GitHub repo ejejejdfbbebe/nodejs.org fork (dash.css file). Malware parses poem to extract 4 words/phrases via pattern matching ('In the silent hum of X,', 'each pulse of X threading', 'Beyond the wall of X,', 'the X servers'), converts words to numbers via hardcoded dictionary, combines to form IPv4 C2 address. Deploys XMRig and Iron crypto miners connecting to Kryptex (5.180.174.162). Converts victims into HTTP/S scanners and exploit servers for expansion. Poem updated 11 times since Apr 13, 2026 to rotate C2. Italian-speaking actor. 3,400+ victims, peak 800 active/day, predominantly US/Western Europe.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Canto Incognito campaign; Italian-speaking threat actor (assessment); financially motivated cryptocurrency mining operation

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Exploitation of publicly exposed vulnerable services: LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520; first activity April 2026
- Victims and sectors: 3,400+ victim servers; enterprise AI infrastructure; development toolkits; predominantly US and Western Europe; peak activity 800 active servers per day
- Regions: United States, Europe
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Active since April 2026; 3,400+ impacted servers; peak ~2,200 affected servers mid-June, ~800 active per day; first C2 commit Apr 13, 2026; poem updated 11 times; broader scanning/exploitation began May 2026; recent traffic suggests distributed brute-force experiments

## Attack flow
### vuln-exploit: Exploit vulnerable AI/LLM services (access)

Target publicly exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea, possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520; Gotenberg docs explicitly warn not to expose to internet

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### poem-c2: GitHub poem-derived C2 (execution)

Malware queries GitHub repo ejejejdfbbebe/nodejs.org fork for dash.css; parses poem 'On the Nature of Connection' to extract 4 words ('In the silent hum of X', 'each pulse of X threading', 'Beyond the wall of X', 'the X servers'); converts words to numbers via hardcoded dictionary; combines to IPv4 C2 address; poem updated 11 times since Apr 13, 2026

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### deploy-malware: Deploy libgcrypt malware (execution)

Downloads and executes ELF 'libgcrypt' from C2; malware includes remote shell, XMRig and Iron crypto miners, HTTP/S scanning capabilities, exploit deployment

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### mining: Cryptocurrency mining (ai)

Deploys XMRig and Iron miners; connects to Kryptex mining service at 5.180.174.162; GPU hardware attractive target for mining

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### expand-botnet: Convert victims to scanners (impact)

Infected servers become HTTP/S vulnerability scanners and exploit servers; proxy attacks through compromised hosts to expand botnet; repurposed routers for C2 infrastructure; recent experiments with distributed brute-force

Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

### Connections

- vuln-exploit -> poem-c2
- poem-c2 -> deploy-malware
- deploy-malware -> mining
- deploy-malware -> expand-botnet
- expand-botnet -> vuln-exploit [loop]

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0010](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0010) AI Supply Chain Compromise — Supply chain-style targeting of exposed AI/LLM services (LiteLLM, Ollama) for compromise and cryptocurrency mining
  Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>
- [AML.T0034](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0034) Cost Harvesting — Exploitation of vulnerabilities in AI/LLM infrastructure (possibly Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520, vulnerable LiteLLM/Ollama versions)
  Evidence: <https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware>

## Prevention
Do not expose AI/LLM services to internet (Gotenberg guidance explicit); vulnerability patching for LiteLLM/Ollama/Gitea/Ivanti Sentry; monitor for crypto mining (Kryptex 5.180.174.162); GitHub repository monitoring; C2 poem pattern detection; HTTP scanning from AI servers; GPU utilization anomalies

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- LiteLLM
- [Ollama](https://github.com/ollama/ollama)

### Other tooling
- PoeLLM malware (libgcrypt)
- XMRig crypto miner
- Iron crypto miner
- Kryptex mining service
- GitHub for C2 poem hosting
- Gotenberg (PDF converter)
- Gitea (software development toolkit)
- Ivanti Sentry (possibly CVE-2026-10520)

## Source notes
Black Lotus Labs discovered via Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 investigation; disrupted campaign, blocked C2 traffic; Lumen Defender customers protected; malware includes remote shell, miners, HTTP/S scanning, exploit deployment; Gotenberg installation guide warns not to expose to internet

## Sources
- [Canto incognito: tracking the PoeLLM malware](https://www.lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-incognito-tracking-the-poellm-malware)
