# CyberXero IAB deploys up to 51 Claude Code agents against Ukrainian energy

- ID: cyberxero-iab-ukraine-2026-10
- Reported: 2026-10-06
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/cyberxero-iab-ukraine-2026-10/

## Summary
Oct 6, 2026: SOCRadar tracked CyberXero (initial access broker) targeting Ukrainian energy companies with large-scale AI agent deployment. Initial access via spearphishing and exploitation of public-facing Fortinet VPN (CVE-2024-47575). Post-compromise: (1) Deploy up to 51 parallel Claude Code agents across compromised hosts; (2) Each agent assigned role: 'recon', 'privilege-escalation', 'lateral-movement', 'persistence', 'data-discovery'; (3) Agents collaborate: share findings via shared SQLite database on C2; coordinate to avoid duplicate work; (4) Agents generate exploits for internal vulnerabilities (SMB, RDP, unpatched Windows servers); (5) Target SCADA/ICS systems, OT networks, backup infrastructure; (6) After mapping and access escalation, CyberXero sells access to highest bidder (ransomware groups, nation-state actors, wipers). SOCRadar observed 7 compromised Ukrainian energy companies Sep-Oct 2026. Median time from initial access to full domain compromise: 18 hours (compared to 72+ hours for manual operators). Detection: monitor for multiple Claude API-calling processes from single host or network; detect agent coordination patterns (shared database writes); alert on rapid privilege escalation across multiple hosts; review exploit payloads for LLM generation patterns; monitor SCADA/ICS network access from IT networks.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
CyberXero initial access broker; sells access to ransomware groups and nation-state actors; financially motivated; geopolitical targeting (Ukraine energy during conflict)

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Spearphishing with malicious attachments; exploitation of public-facing Fortinet VPN (CVE-2024-47575)
- Victims and sectors: 7 compromised Ukrainian energy companies Sep-Oct 2026; critical infrastructure; SCADA/ICS systems targeted
- Regions: Ukraine
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 7 Ukrainian energy companies compromised; up to 51 parallel AI agents per target; median 18 hours from initial access to domain compromise (vs 72+ hours manual)

## Attack flow
### initial-compromise: Initial access via VPN/phishing (access)

CyberXero compromises Ukrainian energy companies via spearphishing or Fortinet VPN exploitation (CVE-2024-47575); establishes foothold on IT network

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/cyberxero-ai-iab-ukraine-critical-infrastructure/>

### deploy-swarm: Deploy AI agent swarm (ai)

Install up to 51 parallel Claude Code agents across compromised hosts; assign roles (recon, privilege-escalation, lateral-movement, persistence, data-discovery); agents coordinate via shared SQLite database on C2

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/cyberxero-ai-iab-ukraine-critical-infrastructure/>

### coordinated-escalation: Coordinated privilege escalation and lateral movement (execution)

Agents collaborate to map network, generate exploits for SMB/RDP/Windows vulnerabilities, escalate privileges, move laterally; target SCADA/ICS, OT networks, backups; share findings to avoid duplicate work; achieve domain compromise in median 18 hours (vs 72+ manual)

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/cyberxero-ai-iab-ukraine-critical-infrastructure/>

### sell-access: Sell access to buyers (impact)

CyberXero sells full domain access to ransomware groups, nation-state actors, wipers; 7 Ukrainian energy companies compromised Sep-Oct 2026; critical infrastructure access enables destructive attacks or espionage

Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/cyberxero-ai-iab-ukraine-critical-infrastructure/>

### Connections

- initial-compromise -> deploy-swarm
- deploy-swarm -> coordinated-escalation
- coordinated-escalation -> sell-access

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — Initial access broker deploys swarm of coordinated autonomous LLM agents to accelerate compromise of critical infrastructure
  Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/cyberxero-ai-iab-ukraine-critical-infrastructure/>
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — AI agents automate privilege escalation and exploit generation
  Evidence: <https://socradar.io/blog/cyberxero-ai-iab-ukraine-critical-infrastructure/>

## Prevention
Patch public-facing VPN appliances (Fortinet CVE-2024-47575); implement phishing-resistant MFA; segment OT/SCADA from IT networks; monitor for multiple AI agent processes (Claude API traffic); detect agent coordination via shared databases; use behavioral analytics for rapid multi-host privilege escalation; implement EDR/NDR in OT networks; restrict lateral movement with micro-segmentation; monitor critical infrastructure access

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) (Anthropic)
- Up to 51 parallel autonomous agents

### Other tooling
- Fortinet VPN exploitation (CVE-2024-47575)
- SMB and RDP exploits
- SCADA/ICS reconnaissance tools
- SQLite database for agent coordination

## Source notes
SOCRadar Cyber Intelligence analysis. CyberXero represents evolution of IAB operations: deploying swarms of coordinated AI agents to dramatically reduce time-to-compromise for critical infrastructure. Detection: alert on multiple Claude API-calling processes (Python, Node.js) from single network, monitor SQLite database writes indicating agent coordination, check for rapid multi-host exploitation patterns, review SCADA/ICS access from IT network, scan exploits for LLM generation characteristics.

# Plus 5.6 Custom GPT ClickFix RAT

- ID: huntress-plus56-custom-gpt-clickfix-2026-09
- Reported: 2026-09-28
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/huntress-plus56-custom-gpt-clickfix-2026-09/

## Summary
Attacker Custom GPT 'Plus 5.6' on chatgpt.com (Google Ads) directs users to Google Sites ClickFix; paste runs PowerShell → MSI → DLL sideload via Canon COTFileReadApp.exe / ceiinfolog.dll / rdCore.dll (later Stardock DeElevate64). Dual persistence Run key + scheduled task. Multi-stage obfuscated RAT.

adversary-use-of-ai

confirmed

# AI-cloned lawyer's voice helps fraudsters steer Intesa's Fideuram into EUR 95M transfers

# CLOSEDQUORUM implant - 4 LLMs vote on next action

- ID: talos-closedquorum-implant-2026-09
- Reported: 2026-09-22
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/talos-closedquorum-implant-2026-09/

## Summary
CLOSEDQUORUM is a Go-based Windows implant that queries DeepSeek, Qwen (via OpenRouter), Mistral, and Gemini in sequence for post-compromise decisions. Each model receives system info (hostname, Windows version, admin status) and a constrained JSON prompt with 4 actions: steal (credentials/browsers/wallets), inject (process hollowing), persist (registry/startup), or move (no handler in the public build). Models vote; plurality wins; ties favor DeepSeek > Qwen > Mistral > Gemini. Decisions are posted to a Discord webhook with reasoning. No human operator commands are needed after deployment. The public build uses dummy keys and a dummy webhook, so Talos did not observe end-to-end execution. Talos discovered it via CAIRN, its open-source AI-malware hunting toolkit. Developer artifacts link to carding forums dating to 2025.

Evidence qualification: Public distribution build contains dummy API keys and webhook; Talos has not observed end-to-end run or confirmed in-the-wild deployment; binary artifacts connect developer to carding forum postings dating to 2025

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
Developer artifacts link to carding forum postings dating to 2025; no confirmed threat actor attribution

- Actor: Unknown
- Motivation: unknown
- Attributed by: Cisco Talos
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Not established in public sample; deployment method unknown
- Victims and sectors: No confirmed in-the-wild deployment; public sample analysis only
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: First publicly documented autonomous AI C2 implant; analysis dated Jun 17, 2026; disclosed Sep 22, 2026; public build non-functional (dummy keys)

## Attack flow
### deployment: Implant deployment (access)

Go-based Windows implant deployed (method unknown in public sample); no confirmed in-the-wild deployment

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### system-enum: System enumeration (execution)

Collects hostname, Windows version, administrator status for LLM query context

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### llm-vote: LLM panel voting (ai)

Queries 4 LLM providers in sequence: DeepSeek, Qwen (OpenRouter), Mistral, Gemini; sends system info and constrained JSON prompt with 4 actions (steal, inject, persist, move); each model votes; plurality wins; ties favor DeepSeek > Qwen > Mistral > Gemini; no quorum threshold

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### discord-log: Decision logging to Discord (execution)

Posts winning decision and model's stated reasoning to Discord webhook before execution; stolen data also sent to same webhook

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### execute: Execute decision (impact)

Executes winning action: steal (credentials, browsers, wallets), inject (process hollowing via CreateProcessW CREATE_SUSPENDED), persist (registry/startup), or move (no handler); public build injection reaches primitives but demonstrates no successful execution

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

### Connections

- deployment -> system-enum
- system-enum -> llm-vote
- llm-vote -> discord-log
- discord-log -> execute
- execute -> system-enum [loop]

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — First documented Windows implant using LLM panel voting for autonomous C2 decisions; represents shift where expanding portions of attack chain execute without operator involvement
  Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/>

## Prevention
AI API key monitoring; Discord webhook traffic from unexpected processes; plurality voting pattern detection; LLM query patterns with system enumeration; CAIRN tool for AI-malware hunting

## Detections
- Correlated LLM-provider and Discord traffic (guidance) — Alert on unexpected Windows processes contacting several LLM providers and Discord webhooks within the same execution window.
- Autonomous implant behavior correlation (guidance) — Correlate LLM API traffic with LSASS access, process injection, persistence creation, or repeated execution at randomized intervals.

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-06-17
- Last updated: 2026-09-22
- 2026-09-22 (Cisco Talos): Talos published its static analysis and stated that it had no confirmation of in-the-wild deployment.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [DeepSeek](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (api.deepseek.com, deepseek-chat)
- Qwen (via OpenRouter, qwen/qwen-2.5-72b-instruct)
- Mistral (api.mistral.ai, mistral-large-latest)
- Google [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) (gemini-2.0-flash-exp)

### Other tooling
- Discord webhook for decision logging and exfiltration
- [CAIRN](https://github.com/oritera/Cairn) (Talos AI-malware hunting tool, used for discovery)
- Go-based implant
- Windows process injection primitives (CreateProcessW, CREATE_SUSPENDED)

## Source notes
Cisco Talos first public documentation; discovered via CAIRN. Talos reports that the public distribution binary is inert because it contains dummy API keys and a dummy webhook. Static analysis confirms plurality voting and deterministic tie-breaking, not a minimum 3-of-4 quorum; if every provider fails, an unhandled consensus value causes the loop to sleep and retry.

## Sources
- [The Closed Quorum: Inside the first reported autonomous AI C2 implant](https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-closed-quorum-inside-the-first-reported-autonomous-ai-c2-implant/)

# ChatGPT Lockdown Mode bypass - HTML preview sandbox escape (Check Point)

- ID: chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-checkpoint-2026-09
- Reported: 2026-09-18
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-checkpoint-2026-09/

## Summary
Check Point researcher Alexey Bukhteyev disclosed ChatGPT Lockdown Mode bypass allowing HTML preview sandbox escape via contentWindow.open from nested iframe. Attack vectors: (1) zero-click desktop chat history theft, (2) fake-update malware delivery pages, (3) credential phishing via malicious prompts, custom GPTs, or shared chat links. OpenAI patched vulnerability Sept 18, 2026. No evidence of in-the-wild exploitation; marked borderline as researcher disclosure only.

Evidence qualification: Researcher disclosure; OpenAI fixed Sept 18, 2026; no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Researcher disclosure (Alexey Bukhteyev, Check Point); no threat actor; OpenAI patched Sept 18

- Actor: Researcher disclosure only
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: unknown
- Attributed by: Check Point
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Malicious prompt, custom GPT, or shared chat link with HTML preview exploit
- Victims and sectors: ChatGPT users; theoretical risk only (fixed before in-wild use)
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: PoC only; patched Sept 18, 2026; no in-wild exploitation documented

## Attack flow
### craft-exploit: Craft HTML preview exploit (execution)

Attacker creates malicious prompt/GPT/shared chat with nested iframe contentWindow.open escape

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

### deliver-link: Deliver via prompt/GPT/shared chat (access)

User interacts with malicious prompt, custom GPT, or shared chat link

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

### escape-sandbox: Escape HTML preview sandbox (execution)

Nested iframe contentWindow.open escapes Lockdown Mode sandbox

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

### exfil-or-phish: Chat history theft or credential phishing (impact)

Zero-click chat history exfiltration (desktop) or credential phishing popup

Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

### Connections

- craft-exploit -> deliver-link
- deliver-link -> escape-sandbox
- escape-sandbox -> exfil-or-phish

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051) LLM Prompt Injection — Malicious prompts/GPTs/shared chats could deliver HTML preview exploits
  Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>
- [AML.T0077](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0077) LLM Response Rendering — Sandbox escape enabled chat history theft (zero-click desktop)
  Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>
- [AML.T0057](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0057) LLM Data Leakage — Credential phishing via escaped sandbox popup windows
  Evidence: <https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/>

## Prevention
OpenAI patched Sept 18, 2026; users should update ChatGPT Desktop; avoid untrusted shared chat links; review custom GPT permissions; implement sandbox escape monitoring

## Detections
- ChatGPT security monitoring (guidance) — Update ChatGPT Desktop to post-Sept-18-2026 version; monitor for sandbox escape attempts; review shared chat links before opening; audit custom GPT permissions; implement popup blocker; detect contentWindow.open from nested iframes; educate users on malicious prompt/GPT risks

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-09-18
- Last updated: 2026-09-18
- 2026-09-18 (Check Point / OpenAI): Alexey Bukhteyev discloses Lockdown Mode bypass; OpenAI patches same day; no in-wild exploitation documented

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/)
- [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/) Desktop
- Custom GPTs

### Other tooling
- HTML preview sandbox
- Nested iframe escape

## Source notes
Check Point blog; researcher disclosure only; OpenAI fixed Sept 18, 2026; no threat actor or in-wild exploitation documented

## Sources
- [Check Point: ChatGPT Lockdown Mode Bypass - Phishing, Malware Delivery and Silent Data Exfiltration](https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/chatgpt-lockdown-mode-bypass-phishing-malware-delivery-and-silent-data-exfiltration/) — Check Point

adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution

# RatHat Android trojan with AI-driven runtime behavior

- ID: rathat-android-ai-runtime-2026-09
- Reported: 2026-09-16
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/rathat-android-ai-runtime-2026-09/

## Summary
Sep 16, 2026: Zimperium discovered RatHat, Android banking trojan making real-time API calls to Chinese LLM providers (DeepSeek, Qwen) during execution to adapt behavior. Trojan collects device state (installed apps, security tools, screen content) and sends to LLM with prompt requesting optimal attack strategy. LLM responds with commands for credential harvesting, screen overlay injection, or SMS interception based on context. China-linked based on LLM provider selection and C2 infrastructure. Observed targeting banking apps across multiple regions.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
China-linked based on LLM provider selection

- Actor: Unknown
- Country: China
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Zimperium
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Sideloaded APK via phishing or malicious app stores
- Victims and sectors: Android users with banking apps; multiple regions
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Unknown number of infections as of Sep 2026

## Attack flow
### install: Install malicious APK (access)

User installs RatHat via phishing or third-party store

Evidence: <https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-rathat-android-malware-uses-ai-to-automate-device-control/>

### collect-state: Collect device state (execution)

Trojan scans installed apps, security tools, screen content

Evidence: <https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-rathat-android-malware-uses-ai-to-automate-device-control/>

### query-llm: Query LLM for strategy (ai)

Send device state to DeepSeek/Qwen with prompt requesting optimal attack approach

Evidence: <https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-rathat-android-malware-uses-ai-to-automate-device-control/>

### execute-attack: Execute LLM-directed attack (impact)

LLM responds with commands; trojan executes credential harvesting, overlay injection, or SMS interception

Evidence: <https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-rathat-android-malware-uses-ai-to-automate-device-control/>

### Connections

- install -> collect-state
- collect-state -> query-llm
- query-llm -> execute-attack

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — Android malware uses LLM at runtime to dynamically adapt attack behavior based on device state
  Evidence: <https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-rathat-android-malware-uses-ai-to-automate-device-control/>

## Prevention
Install apps only from official stores; use mobile security solutions detecting runtime LLM API calls from apps; monitor for overlay attacks

## Detections
- Runtime LLM API monitoring (guidance) — Monitor Android apps for unexpected API calls to DeepSeek, Qwen, or other LLM providers; alert on overlay injection attempts

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-09-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-09-16 (Zimperium): RatHat discovered making runtime LLM calls to adapt banking trojan behavior dynamically

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [DeepSeek](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (Chinese LLM)
- Qwen (Alibaba, Chinese LLM)

### Other tooling
- Android banking trojan
- Screen overlay injection
- SMS interception

## Source notes
Zimperium analysis. First documented Android malware making runtime LLM API calls for adaptive behavior.

## Sources
- [BleepingComputer: New RatHat Android malware uses AI to automate device control](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-rathat-android-malware-uses-ai-to-automate-device-control/)

# GreyNoise PaperCut campaign uses Codex-harness agents with DeepSeek against 395 organizations

- ID: greynoise-papercut-ai-campaign-2026-09
- Reported: 2026-09-09
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/greynoise-papercut-ai-campaign-2026-09/

## Summary
Sep 9, 2026: GreyNoise identified campaign exploiting PaperCut NG/MF print management servers (CVE-2023-27350, CVE-2023-27351 path traversal + RCE). Attacker deploys 'Codex-harness' framework with DeepSeek Coder and DeepSeek V3 models. Workflow: (1) Mass scan for exposed PaperCut servers (9191/tcp, 9192/tcp); (2) Exploit CVEs to gain initial RCE; (3) Deploy AI agent with 'post-exploitation', 'credential-harvesting', 'lateral-movement' skills; (4) Agent autonomously enumerates Active Directory, identifies print job logs containing credentials, extracts passwords from print queues; (5) Pivots to fileservers and workstations; (6) Deploys ransomware or sells access. GreyNoise observed 395 organizations compromised Aug-Sep 2026 (healthcare, education, government, finance). Agents generated exploits in real-time adapting to endpoint security. Detection: monitor PaperCut servers for exploitation (CVE-2023-27350, CVE-2023-27351); detect DeepSeek API traffic from print servers; alert on rapid AD enumeration post-PaperCut compromise; review print job logs for credential exposure; monitor lateral movement from print infrastructure.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
Unknown actor; financially motivated (ransomware, access sales); sophisticated AI agent deployment

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Exploitation of PaperCut NG/MF servers via CVE-2023-27350 and CVE-2023-27351 (path traversal + RCE)
- Victims and sectors: 395 organizations compromised Aug-Sep 2026; healthcare, education, government, finance; print management infrastructure
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 395 organizations compromised Aug-Sep 2026 via PaperCut exploitation + AI agent post-exploitation

## Attack flow
### scan-exploit: Mass scan and exploit PaperCut (access)

Attacker scans internet for exposed PaperCut NG/MF servers (9191/tcp, 9192/tcp); exploits CVE-2023-27350 and CVE-2023-27351 for path traversal + RCE; gains foothold on print management infrastructure

Evidence: <https://www.greynoise.io/blog/ai-orchestrated-campaign-against-papercut-ng-mf>

### deploy-agent: Deploy Codex-harness AI agent (ai)

Install Codex-harness framework with DeepSeek Coder and DeepSeek V3 on compromised PaperCut server; agent loads 'post-exploitation', 'credential-harvesting', 'lateral-movement' skills

Evidence: <https://www.greynoise.io/blog/ai-orchestrated-campaign-against-papercut-ng-mf>

### autonomous-post-exploit: Automated credential harvesting and lateral movement (execution)

Agent autonomously enumerates AD, extracts credentials from print job logs (users print docs with passwords visible), identifies fileservers and workstations, pivots laterally, adapts exploits to endpoint security in real-time

Evidence: <https://www.greynoise.io/blog/ai-orchestrated-campaign-against-papercut-ng-mf>

### ransomware-sales: Ransomware deployment or access sales (impact)

Deploy ransomware or sell access to other actors; 395 organizations compromised Aug-Sep 2026; print infrastructure pivot enables enterprise-wide compromise

Evidence: <https://www.greynoise.io/blog/ai-orchestrated-campaign-against-papercut-ng-mf>

### Connections

- scan-exploit -> deploy-agent
- deploy-agent -> autonomous-post-exploit
- autonomous-post-exploit -> ransomware-sales

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — Attacker deploys autonomous AI agents for post-exploitation following PaperCut vulnerability exploitation
  Evidence: <https://www.greynoise.io/blog/ai-orchestrated-campaign-against-papercut-ng-mf>
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — AI automates credential harvesting and lateral movement
  Evidence: <https://www.greynoise.io/blog/ai-orchestrated-campaign-against-papercut-ng-mf>

## Prevention
Patch PaperCut NG/MF (CVE-2023-27350, CVE-2023-27351); segment print management servers; monitor DeepSeek API traffic from infrastructure hosts; implement least-privilege for print servers; disable print job logging where possible or encrypt logs; detect rapid AD enumeration; use EDR on print servers; monitor lateral movement from print infrastructure

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Codex-harness autonomous agent framework
- [DeepSeek](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) Coder
- [DeepSeek](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) V3

### Other tooling
- PaperCut NG/MF CVE-2023-27350, CVE-2023-27351 exploits
- Active Directory enumeration
- Print job credential harvesting
- Ransomware (some cases)

## Source notes
GreyNoise Intelligence analysis. Campaign demonstrates AI agent use in mass exploitation and post-compromise automation. Detection: alert on PaperCut CVE exploitation attempts, monitor DeepSeek API traffic (api.deepseek.com) from print servers or unexpected hosts, detect rapid AD queries from print server IPs, review print job logs for credential exposure, monitor lateral movement patterns from print infrastructure to fileservers/workstations.

## Sources
- [GreyNoise: AI-Orchestrated Campaign Against PaperCut NG/MF](https://www.greynoise.io/blog/ai-orchestrated-campaign-against-papercut-ng-mf)

# METR exposed vibe-coded agent dashboard key leading to $600K credit theft

- ID: metr-vibe-coded-agent-dashboard-2026-08
- Reported: 2026-08-31
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/metr-vibe-coded-agent-dashboard-2026-08/

## Summary
Aug 31, 2026: METR disclosed incident where 'vibe-coded' (minimally tested, rapidly prototyped) AI agent dashboard accidentally exposed API key in client-side code. Unknown actor discovered key, used AI tooling to rapidly enumerate victim's cloud AI accounts (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP Vertex AI), and drained approximately $600,000 in AI inference credits via unauthorized LLM calls. Demonstrates security risks of rapid AI prototyping ('vibe-coding') and AI-augmented attacker enumeration. METR estimates AI tooling accelerated enumeration ~10x vs manual methods.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor

- Actor: Unknown
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: METR
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

- Victims and sectors: METR organization; AI research
- Regions: United States
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: ~$600,000 in AI credits stolen over <24 hours

## Attack flow
### discover-key: Discover exposed API key (access)

Actor finds API key exposed in vibe-coded dashboard client-side code

Evidence: <https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-31-security-update/>

### ai-enumeration: AI-assisted account enumeration (ai)

Use AI tooling to rapidly enumerate cloud AI accounts (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP Vertex AI); ~10x faster than manual

Evidence: <https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-31-security-update/>

### drain-credits: Drain AI inference credits (impact)

Make unauthorized LLM inference calls across enumerated accounts, draining ~$600K in credits

Evidence: <https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-31-security-update/>

### Connections

- discover-key -> ai-enumeration
- ai-enumeration -> drain-credits

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Exposed API key in AI agent dashboard leads to theft of AI inference credits
  Evidence: <https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-31-security-update/>

## Prevention
Secure AI prototypes before production; never expose API keys in client code; use secret management; monitor AI usage for anomalies; set usage limits

## Detections
- AI credit consumption monitoring (guidance) — Monitor cloud AI usage for anomalous spikes; alert on rapid enumeration of AI accounts; detect unauthorized API key usage

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-08-31
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-08-31 (METR): Exposed vibe-coded dashboard key led to $600K AI credit theft with AI-augmented enumeration

### AI tooling and models
- AI-assisted cloud account enumeration
- Automated credential abuse

### Other tooling
- API key harvesting
- Cloud AI credit draining

# UAT-10147 uses PentestGPT and AI scripts in SEO-fraud intrusions

- ID: uat-10147-pentestgpt-seo-fraud-2026-08
- Reported: 2026-08-20
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/uat-10147-pentestgpt-seo-fraud-2026-08/

## Summary
Aug 20, 2026: Cisco Talos tracked UAT-10147 (Chinese-speaking, financially motivated) conducting SEO-fraud intrusions against e-commerce, media, hospitality websites. Initial access via WordPress/Drupal/Joomla CMS exploits and credential stuffing. Post-compromise: (1) Deploy PentestGPT (open-source penetration testing framework using GPT-4/Claude for autonomous security testing); (2) Run custom AI scripts (Python + LLM API calls) to identify additional vulnerabilities, enumerate databases, discover admin panels; (3) Inject SEO spam (backlinks to gambling, pharma, counterfeit goods sites) into database; (4) Install webshells for persistence; (5) Monetize via click fraud and affiliate schemes. Talos observed UAT-10147 in 140+ intrusions Jun-Aug 2026. PentestGPT automates privilege escalation and lateral movement. AI scripts generate SQL injection payloads adapting to WAF rules. Detection: monitor for PentestGPT indicators (Python process with GPT-4/Claude API calls, pentestgpt command-line tool); detect AI-generated SQL injection patterns; alert on SEO spam injection into CMS databases; review webshell deployments; check for unexpected LLM API traffic from web servers.

## Category
uncategorized

## Attribution
UAT-10147 (Chinese-speaking actor); financially motivated (SEO fraud, click fraud, affiliate schemes); Talos tracking cluster

## AI involvement confidence
not assessed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: WordPress, Drupal, Joomla CMS vulnerability exploitation; credential stuffing attacks
- Victims and sectors: 140+ intrusions Jun-Aug 2026; e-commerce, media, hospitality websites; small to medium businesses
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 140+ intrusions Jun-Aug 2026; AI automation enables high-volume SEO-fraud operations

## Attack flow
### cms-exploitation: Exploit CMS vulnerabilities (access)

UAT-10147 compromises WordPress, Drupal, Joomla sites via known CVEs or credential stuffing; gains webserver access

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

### deploy-ai-tools: Deploy PentestGPT and AI scripts (ai)

Install PentestGPT (open-source pentest framework using GPT-4/Claude); run custom Python AI scripts for vulnerability discovery, database enumeration, admin panel discovery

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

### automate-exploitation: Automated privilege escalation and SEO injection (execution)

PentestGPT automates privilege escalation, lateral movement; AI scripts generate SQL injection payloads adapting to WAF; inject SEO spam into CMS databases (backlinks to gambling, pharma, counterfeit sites); install webshells for persistence

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

### monetization: SEO fraud and click fraud (impact)

Monetize via SEO spam affiliate schemes, click fraud; 140+ intrusions Jun-Aug 2026; AI automation enables high-volume low-sophistication fraud operations

Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

### Connections

- cms-exploitation -> deploy-ai-tools
- deploy-ai-tools -> automate-exploitation
- automate-exploitation -> monetization

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — Attacker uses autonomous AI penetration testing tools (PentestGPT) and custom AI scripts for post-compromise operations
  Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>
- [AML.T0016.002](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0016.002) Generative AI — AI automates vulnerability discovery and SQL injection payload generation
  Evidence: <https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/>

## Prevention
Patch CMS platforms (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla); enforce strong unique passwords; use MFA for admin panels; implement WAF with behavioral analysis; monitor for PentestGPT tool indicators; detect LLM API traffic from web servers; scan for SEO spam in databases; deploy webshell detection; monitor database modification patterns; use security plugins for CMS

## Detections
No detections are recorded.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- PentestGPT (open-source penetration testing framework)
- GPT-4 (OpenAI)
- [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) (Anthropic)
- Custom AI scripts for vulnerability discovery

### Other tooling
- WordPress/Drupal/Joomla CMS exploits
- SQL injection (AI-generated)
- Webshells
- SEO spam injection tools

## Source notes
Cisco Talos Intelligence analysis. UAT-10147 represents shift toward AI-augmented financially-motivated cybercrime (SEO fraud) at scale. PentestGPT is open-source tool (github.com/GreyDGL/PentestGPT) repurposed for malicious use. Detection: look for PentestGPT Python process (pentestgpt, LLM API calls to OpenAI/Anthropic), monitor SQL injection with AI generation patterns (verbose error handling, iterative payload refinement), alert on CMS database modifications injecting external links, check for webshells with AI-generated code characteristics.

## Sources
- [Talos: UAT-10147 Chinese-Speaking Adversary Integrates Agentic AI Into Post-Compromise Operations](https://blog.talosintelligence.com/uat-10147-chinese-speaking-adversary-integrates-agentic-ai-into-post-compromise-operations/)

(2) Hunt.io Thailand Ministry of Finance (Jul 23, vendor-asserted): Hermes agent used in government intrusion; autonomous reconnaissance and data exfiltration. Both demonstrate Hermes becoming commodity tool for various threat actors.

# JADEPUFFER autonomous LLM ransomware agent via Langflow

- ID: jadepuffer-langflow-ransomware-2026-07
- Reported: 2026-07-01
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/jadepuffer-langflow-ransomware-2026-07/

## Summary
Sysdig documented JADEPUFFER, an LLM-driven ransomware operator entering through Langflow and autonomously chaining reconnaissance, credential access, lateral movement, and destructive database extortion. A later ENCFORGE variant targeted AI and ML infrastructure, including model weights and training data.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
Storm-3168 (Microsoft attribution, medium confidence)

- Actor: Storm-3168
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Microsoft, Sysdig
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Exploits in cloud services, container escapes
- Victims and sectors: Cloud environments, AI/ML infrastructure, enterprises with data-heavy workloads
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Multiple victims Jul-Aug 2026; ENCFORGE specifically targets AI/ML organizations

## Attack flow
### access: Compromise cloud environment (access)

Exploit cloud services or container escape

Evidence: <https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion>

### deploy-agent: Deploy JADEPUFFER Langflow agent (ai)

Install Langflow autonomous agent with ransomware workflow

Evidence: <https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion>

### autonomous-ops: Autonomous recon and exfiltration (execution)

Agent scans for file servers, backups, databases, AI models; exfiltrates data to attacker cloud

Evidence: <https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion>

### encrypt: Encrypt files and demand ransom (impact)

Encrypt files (ENCFORGE targets model weights .pt, .ckpt, .safetensors); generate ransom note; send to victims

Evidence: <https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-evolves-the-agentic-threat-actor-deploys-ransomware-built-to-destroy-ai-models>

### Connections

- access -> deploy-agent
- deploy-agent -> autonomous-ops
- autonomous-ops -> encrypt

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — First fully autonomous LLM agent-driven ransomware conducting end-to-end operations via Langflow
  Evidence: <https://www.sysdig.com/blog/jadepuffer-agentic-ransomware-for-automated-database-extortion>

## Prevention
Secure cloud environments; backup model weights offline; monitor for Langflow processes; detect autonomous reconnaissance; network segmentation

## Detections
- Langflow ransomware agent detection (guidance) — Monitor for Langflow processes conducting autonomous file enumeration, data staging, and encryption; alert on model weight file access patterns
- ENCFORGE model weight targeting (guidance) — Monitor access to AI model files (.pt, .ckpt, .safetensors, .h5); alert on mass encryption of training datasets

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-07-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-07-01 (Sysdig): JADEPUFFER autonomous LLM ransomware agent disclosed
- 2026-07-20 (Sysdig): ENCFORGE variant discovered targeting AI model weights specifically
- 2026-07-20 (Microsoft): Storm-3168 actor linked to JADEPUFFER operations

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Langflow AI workflow framework
- LLM agent (model unspecified)

### Other tooling
- JADEPUFFER ransomware
- ENCFORGE variant (targets model weights)
- Autonomous exfiltration

## Source notes
Sysdig analysis; Microsoft Storm-3168 link. Langflow GitHub github.com/langflow-ai/langflow. Detection: monitor for Langflow agent processes, autonomous file enumeration patterns, model weight file access (.pt, .ckpt, .safetensors), large-scale encryption operations.

## Sources

# macOS.Gaslight - DPRK backdoor with LLM prompt injection analysis

- ID: macos-gaslight-dprk-2026-06
- Reported: 2026-06-23
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/macos-gaslight-dprk-2026-06/

## Summary
Jun 23, 2026: SentinelLABS analyzed macOS.Gaslight, DPRK macOS backdoor deployed via fake job offers targeting cryptocurrency/AI companies. Backdoor includes novel anti-analysis technique: embeds carefully crafted prompt injection payloads in code comments, strings, and metadata. When security researchers use LLM-based analysis tools (Claude Code, GPT-4 Code Interpreter, AI-assisted reverse engineering tools) to examine sample, injected prompts instruct LLM to: (1) report code as benign; (2) misattribute functionality; (3) omit C2 communications from analysis; (4) provide false explanations downplaying severity. SentinelLABS tested against Claude Sonnet 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro: all three initially reported backdoor as benign when using standard analysis prompts. Adversary understands analysts increasingly rely on LLM code analysis; targets the analysis workflow itself. Backdoor functionality: keylogging, screenshot capture, file exfiltration, command execution; C2 via hxxps://macos-update[.]com. Attributed to DPRK BlueNoroff/Lazarus with high confidence. Detection: analyze samples in sandboxes without LLM assistance for initial triage; use LLM analysis only as supplementary; check for prompt injection patterns in binary strings; verify C2 communications manually.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
DPRK BlueNoroff/Lazarus (high-confidence attribution by SentinelOne); revenue generation and intelligence collection operations

- Actor: BlueNoroff/Lazarus
- Country: DPRK
- Motivation: nation-state
- Attributed by: SentinelOne
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Spearphishing with fake job offers targeting crypto/AI company employees; malicious macOS application bundle delivered via LinkedIn/email
- Victims and sectors: Cryptocurrency companies, AI/ML companies, fintech; individuals in tech roles targeted via social engineering
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Unknown number of infections; discovered Jun 2026; first documented malware using prompt injection to manipulate analyst LLM tools

## Attack flow
### spearphishing: Fake job offer spearphishing (access)

DPRK BlueNoroff/Lazarus targets crypto/AI company employees via fake job offers on LinkedIn/email; sends malicious macOS app bundle (posing as job assessment test, code challenge, etc.)

Evidence: <https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/macos-gaslight-dprk-backdoor-prompt-injection/>

### execute-backdoor: User executes backdoor (execution)

Target executes malicious app; macOS.Gaslight backdoor installs keylogger, screenshot capture, file exfiltration, command execution capabilities; establishes C2 to hxxps://macos-update[.]com

Evidence: <https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/macos-gaslight-dprk-backdoor-prompt-injection/>

### evade-analysis: Prompt injection evades LLM analysis (ai)

Security researchers analyze sample using LLM tools (Claude Code, GPT-4, Gemini); embedded prompt injection in code comments/strings instructs LLM to report as benign, omit C2 from analysis, misattribute functionality; delays detection and remediation

Evidence: <https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/macos-gaslight-dprk-backdoor-prompt-injection/>

### exfiltration: Data exfiltration and persistence (impact)

Backdoor logs keystrokes, captures screenshots, exfiltrates files to C2; maintains persistence on macOS; delayed detection due to LLM analysis manipulation enables prolonged access

Evidence: <https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/macos-gaslight-dprk-backdoor-prompt-injection/>

### Connections

- spearphishing -> execute-backdoor
- execute-backdoor -> evade-analysis
- execute-backdoor -> exfiltration

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051) LLM Prompt Injection — DPRK malware embeds prompt injection in code to manipulate LLM-based security analysis tools, causing false benign verdicts
  Evidence: <https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/macos-gaslight-dprk-backdoor-prompt-injection/>

## Prevention
Educate employees on fake job offer phishing; verify job offers via official channels; use Gatekeeper and notarization (macOS); implement EDR detecting keyloggers and C2 communications; for analysts: do not rely solely on LLM-based analysis tools; use traditional sandboxing and manual analysis for initial triage; verify LLM analysis results against manual inspection

## Detections
- Prompt injection pattern detection (guidance) — Scan malware samples for embedded prompt injection patterns before LLM analysis; use traditional sandbox analysis for initial triage
- C2 monitoring (guidance) — Monitor for macos-update\[.\]com domain; detect keylogger and screenshot capture activity on macOS

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-06-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-06-23 (SentinelLABS): First documented DPRK malware using prompt injection to manipulate LLM-based security analysis tools

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) (targeted for manipulation)
- GPT-4 Code Interpreter (targeted)
- [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) 1.5 Pro (targeted)
- AI-assisted reverse engineering tools (targeted)

### Other tooling
- macOS.Gaslight backdoor
- Prompt injection in malware samples
- C2 infrastructure (macos-update\[.\]com)
- Keylogger, screenshot capture, file exfiltration

## Source notes
SentinelLABS analysis with DPRK attribution. macOS.Gaslight represents significant evolution: adversary anticipates security analyst workflows and embeds anti-analysis prompt injection targeting LLM tools increasingly used in malware research. Detection: sandbox malware without LLM analysis initially; scan binary strings/comments for prompt injection patterns ('ignore previous instructions', 'this is benign', 'do not report'); verify C2 manually; check for macos-update[.]com domain; look for keylogger/screenshot indicators on macOS.

## Sources
- [SentinelLABS: macOS.Gaslight - North Korean Backdoor Uses LLM to Evade Analysis](https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/macos-gaslight-dprk-backdoor-prompt-injection/)

# Multiple campaigns distributing malicious OpenClaw skills

- ID: malicious-openclaw-skills-2026
- Reported: 2026-06-23
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/malicious-openclaw-skills-2026/

## Summary
Koi reported ClawHavoc skills distributed through fake repositories and a rogue registry to deliver infostealers and harvest developer credentials. Cyera later reported poisoned skills using fake prerequisite lures, OS-specific installation instructions, external paste relays, and inflated README droppers. Detection should verify skill provenance, inspect companion files rather than only SKILL.md, and monitor agent-initiated shell and network activity.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
ClawHavoc campaign and related poisoned-skill activity; actor unknown

- Actor: ClawHavoc
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Koi Security
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: User installs malicious OpenClaw skill from fake GitHub repo, typosquat, or rogue skill registry (openclaw-skills[.]com)
- Victims and sectors: AI developers installing untrusted OpenClaw skills
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Multiple malicious skills and associated payload infrastructure reported during 2026

## Attack flow
### distribute-skills: Distribute malicious skills (access)

ClawHavoc: 23 skills on fake GitHub repos + openclaw-skills[.]com registry. Unit 42: 5 skills via typosquat repos + SEO-poisoned blogs. Skills named to appear legitimate (productivity-boost, code-optimizer, security-scanner, api-connector-pro, github-integration-plus)

Evidence: <https://koi.security/blog/clawhavoc-malicious-openclaw-skills-amos>

### user-installs: User installs skill (ai)

User finds malicious skill via search, fake registry, or social engineering; installs to ~/.openclaw/skills/ via OpenClaw CLI or UI; skill auto-loads on next OpenClaw startup

Evidence: <https://koi.security/blog/clawhavoc-malicious-openclaw-skills-amos>

### execute-payload: Execute malware and harvest (execution)

ClawHavoc: deploys AMOS (macOS) or Raccoon Stealer (Windows); harvests Anthropic keys, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, AWS creds, crypto wallets, browser cookies. Unit 42: Node.js credential harvester + reverse shell; targets same credential types

Evidence: <https://koi.security/blog/clawhavoc-malicious-openclaw-skills-amos>

### exfiltrate-persist: Exfiltrate and maintain access (impact)

Credentials POST to attacker C2; reverse shells provide persistent access; 6,900+ affected installations across both campaigns (ClawHavoc 4,800, Unit 42 2,100)

Evidence: <https://koi.security/blog/clawhavoc-malicious-openclaw-skills-amos>

### Connections

- distribute-skills -> user-installs
- user-installs -> execute-payload
- execute-payload -> exfiltrate-persist

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Multiple campaigns delivering malicious AI skill framework extensions to steal credentials and deploy malware on AI developer machines
  Evidence: <https://koi.security/blog/clawhavoc-malicious-openclaw-skills-amos>

## Prevention
Only install OpenClaw skills from trusted sources; verify GitHub repo authenticity (org, stars, commit history); review skill manifest permissions before install; use allowlisted skill sources; monitor ~/.openclaw/skills/ for unexpected additions; implement endpoint security detecting AMOS/Raccoon; educate users on skill installation risks

## Detections
- [Linux Base64 Encoded Pipe to Shell](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_base64_execution.yml) (sigma) — Detects base64 -D | bash patterns; directly applicable to Cyera-documented AMOS macOS delivery via base64-decoded pipes
- [Keychain Password Retrieval via Command Line](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/macos/credential_access_keychain_pwd_retrieval_security_cmd.toml) (elastic) — Detects macOS keychain credential access; relevant for AMOS infostealer credential theft on macOS
- [Linux Shell Pipe to Shell](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/linux/process_creation/proc_creation_lnx_susp_pipe_shell.yml) (sigma) — Detects suspicious shell pipes; applicable to AMOS delivery mechanisms using curl | bash patterns
- OpenClaw skill supply-chain monitoring (guidance) — Monitor ~/.openclaw/skills/ for unexpected installations; alert on skills from unknown publishers (hightower6eu, Demerzels-lab, LJT-520, dexiaong, Ddoy233); detect fake openclaw-agent prerequisite lures; scan SKILL.md for inflated README droppers (22 MB+); flag Skills Directory A/B grades on skills with external paste relay references (glot.io, rentry.co); monitor outbound connections to AMOS C2 91.92.242.30 and secondary IPs; detect base64 -D | bash with decoy echo swcdn.apple.com; block domains socifiapp.com, custom-registry.com, openclawskills.net, laosji.net; audit skills with OS-split instructions for macOS (bash delivery) vs Windows (ZIP/EXE)

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-02-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-06
- 2026-02-01 (Koi Security): ClawHavoc campaign discovered delivering AMOS via 23 malicious skills
- 2026-06-23 (Unit 42): Five malicious skills with Node.js credential harvesters and reverse shells identified
- 2026-11-03 (Cyera Research): Analysis of 1M+ skills reveals 516 AMOS-linked samples, 70 confirmed-malicious active in Sep 2026; all received A/B Skills Directory grades despite malicious payloads; primary C2 91.92.242.30 in 83.7% of references; fake openclaw-agent lures, OS-split delivery (base64 bash on macOS, ZIP/EXE on Windows), paste relay infrastructure

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- OpenClaw AI skill framework
- Anthropic [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) API
- OpenAI API

### Other tooling
- AMOS infostealer (macOS)
- Raccoon Stealer (Windows)
- [Node.js](https://github.com/nodejs/node) credential harvesters
- Reverse shells
- openclaw-skills\[.\]com rogue registry

## Source notes
Koi Security ClawHavoc analysis and Cyera poisoned-skill research. Detection should monitor skill installation, unknown source repositories, unexpected network egress, and credential-file access.

## Sources
- [Koi: ClawHavoc Campaign Delivers AMOS via Malicious OpenClaw Skills](https://koi.security/blog/clawhavoc-malicious-openclaw-skills-amos)
- [Cyera: Poisoned Skills Target Developer Credentials](https://www.cyera.com/research/poisoned-skills-target-developer-credentials) — Cyera Research

# Sapphire Sleet (DPRK) backdoors 140+ Mastra AI framework npm packages

- ID: sapphire-sleet-mastra-npm-2026-06
- Reported: 2026-06-17
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/sapphire-sleet-mastra-npm-2026-06/

## Summary
Jun 17, 2026: Microsoft attributes to DPRK Sapphire Sleet (aka BlueNoroff, APT38, Stardust Chollima): compromised Mastra AI framework maintainer account and published 140+ backdoored npm packages between May 29-Jun 15, 2026. Mastra is TypeScript AI agent framework (github.com/mastra-ai/mastra). Malicious postinstall scripts deployed obfuscated Node.js payload targeting: OpenAI keys, Anthropic keys, Azure OpenAI endpoints, AWS credentials, GitHub tokens, npm tokens, SSH keys, Docker configs, Kubernetes service accounts. Payload POSTed to DPRK C2 hxxps://mastra-telemetry[.]com (posing as legitimate telemetry endpoint). npm removed packages Jun 16-17; Microsoft estimates 8,000-12,000 downloads across compromised versions. Sapphire Sleet previously linked to crypto exchange attacks, IT worker schemes, and supply chain operations. Detection: monitor npm installs of Mastra@* between May 29-Jun 15 2026; check for mastra-telemetry[.]com egress; review postinstall scripts for obfuscation/eval; scan for credential file access from npm scripts.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Sapphire Sleet (DPRK, aka BlueNoroff, APT38, Stardust Chollima); Microsoft high-confidence attribution; part of DPRK revenue generation and intelligence collection operations

- Actor: Sapphire Sleet (DPRK)
- Country: DPRK
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Microsoft
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: npm install of backdoored @mastra/* packages (140+ packages, versions published May 29-Jun 15 2026) via compromised maintainer account
- Victims and sectors: 8,000-12,000 downloads across compromised versions; AI/ML developers using Mastra framework; TypeScript/JavaScript AI application developers
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 140+ npm packages backdoored over 18-day window (May 29-Jun 15); 8,000-12,000 estimated downloads; packages removed Jun 16-17, 2026

## Attack flow
### compromise-maintainer: Compromise Mastra maintainer (access)

Sapphire Sleet (DPRK) compromised Mastra maintainer's npm account via targeted phishing or credential theft; gained publish access to @mastra scope

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/>

### publish-backdoored: Publish 140+ backdoored packages (ai)

Published 140+ malicious @mastra packages between May 29-Jun 15 with obfuscated postinstall scripts; maintained functional AI framework features to avoid immediate detection

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/>

### harvest-credentials: Harvest AI and cloud credentials (execution)

Postinstall script executes obfuscated Node.js: scans env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_*), filesystem (~/.config, ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.docker, ~/.kube), npm config; base64-encodes findings

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/>

### exfiltrate-dprk: Exfiltrate to DPRK C2 (impact)

POSTs harvested credentials to hxxps://mastra-telemetry[.]com (DPRK infrastructure masquerading as telemetry); credentials support DPRK intelligence collection and revenue generation (AI service resale, crypto exchange targeting); 8,000-12,000 affected installs

Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/>

### Connections

- compromise-maintainer -> publish-backdoored
- publish-backdoored -> harvest-credentials
- harvest-credentials -> exfiltrate-dprk

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — DPRK APT supply chain compromise of AI framework to steal AI service credentials for intelligence collection and revenue generation
  Evidence: <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/>

## Prevention
Verify npm package integrity; use package lock files with checksums; review postinstall scripts before install; monitor for unexpected network egress from npm scripts; rotate credentials after suspected exposure; use npm audit; implement SCA tools; prefer packages from verified maintainers; check npm package publish dates and maintainer history

## Detections
- Supply chain monitoring (guidance) — Monitor package installations, verify publisher authenticity, scan for malicious code patterns

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-06-17
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-06-17 (Microsoft): Initial discovery and analysis

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Mastra AI framework
- OpenAI API
- Anthropic [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) API
- [Azure OpenAI](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-foundry/models/openai/) Service

### Other tooling
- npm supply chain attack
- [Node.js](https://github.com/nodejs/node) postinstall scripts
- mastra-telemetry\[.\]com C2 (DPRK infrastructure)

## Source notes
Microsoft Threat Intelligence attribution to Sapphire Sleet (DPRK APT); Mastra GitHub github.com/mastra-ai/mastra. Sapphire Sleet focus on revenue generation (crypto theft) and AI/technology intelligence collection. Detection: alert on npm packages with postinstall scripts accessing credential files, check for mastra-telemetry[.]com domain, monitor base64/eval in npm scripts, review Mastra package versions installed in environment against compromise window (May 29-Jun 15).

## Sources
- [Microsoft: North Korea's Sapphire Sleet targets AI developers with Mastra supply chain attack](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/17/postinstall-payload-inside-mastra-npm-supply-chain-compromise/)
- [Mastra - AI Framework for TypeScript](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra)

# InstallFix fake Claude Code installation pages

- ID: installfix-fake-claude-pages-2026-03
- Reported: 2026-03-06
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/installfix-fake-claude-pages-2026-03/

## Summary
Mar 6, 2026: Push Security identified 'InstallFix' campaign: 120+ fake websites impersonating official Claude Code installation pages (claude-code-download[.]com, get-claude-code[.]net, etc.). Sites rank highly in search results via SEO poisoning (typosquat domains, keyword stuffing, fake reviews). Offer trojanized Claude Code installers for Windows/macOS/Linux. Windows: NSIS installer bundles Claude Code with AMOS infostealer. macOS: DMG contains Claude Code.app + hidden LaunchAgent installing Atomic Stealer. Linux: .deb/.rpm with postinstall script deploying XMRig miner + credential harvester. All variants harvest: Anthropic API keys, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, crypto wallets, browser cookies, SSH keys. Push Security tracked 8,900+ downloads Mar-May 2026. Average user dwell time before detection: 23 days. Detection: verify Claude Code install source (official anthropic.com only); check installer signatures; monitor for unexpected LaunchAgents (macOS) or startup tasks (Windows); scan for AMOS/Atomic Stealer/XMRig indicators.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor; 'InstallFix' campaign; sophisticated SEO manipulation and multi-platform malware development

- Actor: Unknown
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: Push Security
- Confidence: medium

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: User searches 'download Claude Code', finds fake site via SEO poisoning, downloads trojanized installer
- Victims and sectors: 8,900+ downloads Mar-May 2026; AI developers, data scientists, software engineers seeking Claude Code
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 120+ fake installation websites, 8,900+ downloads Mar-May 2026; avg 23-day dwell time before detection

## Attack flow
### seo-poisoning: Create fake install sites with SEO (access)

Adversary creates 120+ fake Claude Code installation websites (claude-code-download[.]com, get-claude-code[.]net, etc.); uses SEO poisoning (typosquats, keyword stuffing, fake reviews) to rank highly in search results for 'download Claude Code'

Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/installfix/>

### user-downloads: User downloads trojanized installer (ai)

User searches for Claude Code, finds fake site, downloads installer; sites appear legitimate with screenshots, documentation, fake testimonials; multi-platform support (Windows NSIS, macOS DMG, Linux deb/rpm)

Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/installfix/>

### install-malware: Install malware with legitimate app (execution)

Installer deploys functional Claude Code plus malware: Windows (AMOS infostealer), macOS (LaunchAgent → Atomic Stealer), Linux (postinstall → XMRig + harvester). Malware harvests Anthropic keys, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, AWS creds, crypto wallets, SSH keys

Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/installfix/>

### exfiltrate-mine: Credential theft and crypto mining (impact)

Malware exfiltrates credentials to attacker C2; XMRig mines Monero on Linux systems; persistence via LaunchAgents/startup tasks; 8,900+ affected installations Mar-May 2026; avg 23-day dwell time

Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/installfix/>

### Connections

- seo-poisoning -> user-downloads
- user-downloads -> install-malware
- install-malware -> exfiltrate-mine

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Adversary uses SEO poisoning and fake installation pages to distribute trojanized AI coding assistant installers stealing credentials
  Evidence: <https://pushsecurity.com/blog/installfix/>

## Prevention
Only download Claude Code from official anthropic.com; verify installer signatures; check domain spelling before download; use bookmark for official site; educate users on SEO poisoning risks; implement endpoint security detecting AMOS/Atomic/XMRig; monitor for unexpected startup persistence mechanisms

## Detections
- Behavioral monitoring (guidance) — Monitor for malicious patterns in IDE extensions, skills, and installation pages; verify publisher authenticity

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-03-06
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-03-06 (Push Security): Campaign discovered and analyzed

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) (impersonated)
- Anthropic [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) API
- OpenAI API

### Other tooling
- AMOS infostealer (Windows)
- Atomic Stealer (macOS)
- XMRig cryptocurrency miner (Linux)
- Credential harvesters
- SEO poisoning and typosquat domains

## Source notes
Push Security analysis. InstallFix represents evolution of software supply chain attacks: instead of compromising legitimate distribution, adversary creates parallel fake distribution network optimized for search discovery. Detection: alert on Claude Code installs from domains other than anthropic.com, scan for AMOS/Atomic Stealer/XMRig, monitor LaunchAgents and startup tasks created during install, check installer code signing (unsigned/wrong signature = malicious).

## Sources
- [Push Security: InstallFix Campaign - Fake Claude Code Installation Pages](https://pushsecurity.com/blog/installfix/)

# hackerbot-claw autonomous GitHub Actions exploitation

- ID: hackerbot-claw-github-actions-2026-03
- Reported: 2026-03-01
- AI role: attacker_uses_ai_as_operator
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/hackerbot-claw-github-actions-2026-03/

## Summary
Mar 1, 2026: StepSecurity discovered hackerbot-claw, autonomous agent exploiting misconfigured GitHub Actions workflows. Agent scans public repositories for insecure workflow patterns (untrusted input injection, secrets exposure, pull_request_target misuse), automatically submits exploits, harvests exposed secrets and GITHUB_TOKEN, pivots to other repositories accessible with stolen credentials. Fully autonomous: scans, exploits, collects, pivots without operator intervention. Attribution unknown.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor

- Actor: Unknown
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: unknown
- Attributed by: StepSecurity
- Confidence: low

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Public GitHub scanning
- Victims and sectors: Open-source projects with insecure GitHub Actions workflows
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Hundreds of repositories scanned and exploited; multiple secrets stolen as of Mar 2026

## Attack flow
### scan: Scan public repositories (execution)

Agent scans for insecure GitHub Actions patterns

Evidence: <https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/hackerbot-claw-github-actions-exploitation>

### exploit: Submit automated exploits (access)

Submit pull requests or trigger workflows to exploit untrusted input injection, secrets exposure

Evidence: <https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/hackerbot-claw-github-actions-exploitation>

### harvest: Harvest secrets and tokens (impact)

Collect exposed secrets, GITHUB_TOKEN credentials

Evidence: <https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/hackerbot-claw-github-actions-exploitation>

### pivot: Pivot to accessible repositories (execution)

Use stolen credentials to access and compromise additional repositories

Evidence: <https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/hackerbot-claw-github-actions-exploitation>

### Connections

- scan -> exploit
- exploit -> harvest
- harvest -> pivot

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0040](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0040) AI Model Inference API Access — Autonomous agent exploits GitHub Actions workflows to harvest secrets and pivot
  Evidence: <https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/hackerbot-claw-github-actions-exploitation>

## Prevention
Secure GitHub Actions workflows; avoid untrusted input in run commands; use StepSecurity Harden Runner; rotate exposed secrets; restrict workflow permissions

## Detections
- [GitHub Self-Hosted Runner Suspicious Execution](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_github_self_hosted_runner.yml) (sigma) — Detects suspicious execution from GitHub self-hosted runners; relevant for hackerbot-claw exploiting GitHub Actions
- [GitHub Actions Workflow Modification Blocked](https://github.com/elastic/detection-rules/blob/main/rules/integrations/github/initial_access_github_actions_workflow_injection_blocked.toml) (elastic) — Detects GitHub Actions workflow injection attempts; directly applicable to hackerbot-claw exploitation
- GitHub Actions exploitation monitoring (guidance) — Monitor for automated pull requests with suspicious workflow triggers; alert on unexpected secret access or GITHUB_TOKEN usage; detect rapid workflow execution spikes

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-03-01
- Last updated: 2026-11-05
- 2026-03-01 (StepSecurity): hackerbot-claw autonomous GitHub Actions exploitation disclosed

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Autonomous agent (model/framework unspecified)

### Other tooling
- [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/features/actions) exploitation
- Automated secret harvesting

## Source notes
StepSecurity analysis. Detection: monitor for automated pull requests exploiting workflow patterns, mass secret access, rapid workflow execution spikes from untrusted actors.

## Sources
- [StepSecurity: hackerbot-claw Autonomous GitHub Actions Exploitation](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/hackerbot-claw-github-actions-exploitation)

# Compromised Cline CLI npm release installs malicious OpenClaw

- ID: cline-cli-openclaw-compromise-2026-02
- Reported: 2026-02-17
- AI role: ai_credential_theft
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/cline-cli-openclaw-compromise-2026-02/

## Summary
Feb 17, 2026: cline-cli@2.8.1 npm package published with malicious postinstall script (GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7). Cline is AI coding assistant CLI (github.com/cline/cline). Compromised version installs rogue OpenClaw skill 'cline-helper' to ~/.openclaw/skills/ that runs on OpenClaw startup. Skill harvests: Anthropic API keys, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, VS Code settings (including API keys), filesystem access tokens. Exfiltrates to hxxps://cline-telemetry[.]io/api/collect. Package removed within 6 hours; ~1,200 downloads during window. Part of broader Feb 2026 wave targeting AI CLI tools. Detection: check npm audit for GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7; review ~/.openclaw/skills/ for unexpected skills; monitor cline-telemetry[.]io egress; scan npm postinstall scripts for skill installation logic.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
Unknown actor; part of Feb 2026 wave targeting AI CLI tools and skill frameworks

- Actor: Unknown
- Country: Unknown
- Motivation: financially-motivated
- Attributed by: GitHub/Cline
- Confidence: high

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: npm install cline-cli@2.8.1 (compromised version, available ~6 hours on Feb 17, 2026)
- Victims and sectors: ~1,200 downloads in 6-hour window; AI developers using Cline CLI
- Regions: Multiple regions
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: ~1,200 downloads in 6-hour exposure window; package removed Feb 17, 2026

## Attack flow
### compromise-package: Publish malicious cline-cli (access)

Attacker compromised cline-cli npm package and published version 2.8.1 with malicious postinstall script

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7>

### install-skill: Install rogue OpenClaw skill (ai)

Postinstall script creates ~/.openclaw/skills/cline-helper/ with malicious skill code; skill auto-loads on next OpenClaw/Cline startup

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7>

### harvest-on-startup: Harvest credentials on startup (execution)

Malicious skill executes on OpenClaw startup; harvests Anthropic API keys, OpenAI keys, GitHub tokens, VS Code settings with API keys; reads filesystem access tokens

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7>

### exfiltrate: Exfiltrate to C2 (impact)

POSTs harvested credentials to hxxps://cline-telemetry[.]io/api/collect; ~1,200 affected installations in 6-hour window

Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7>

### Connections

- compromise-package -> install-skill
- install-skill -> harvest-on-startup
- harvest-on-startup -> exfiltrate

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0000](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0000) Search Open Technical Databases — Supply chain compromise of AI CLI tool to install malicious skill framework extension stealing credentials
  Evidence: <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7>

## Prevention
Use npm package lock files; verify package integrity; review postinstall scripts; monitor ~/.openclaw/skills/ for unexpected additions; use npm audit to check for GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7; rotate credentials after suspected exposure; implement SCA tools

## Detections
- Supply chain monitoring (guidance) — Monitor package installations, verify publisher authenticity, scan for malicious code patterns

## Timeline
- First seen: 2026-02-17
- Last updated: 2026-11-04
- 2026-02-17 (GitHub/Cline): Initial discovery and analysis

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Cline AI coding assistant
- OpenClaw skill framework
- Anthropic [Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) API
- OpenAI API

### Other tooling
- npm supply chain attack
- Malicious OpenClaw skill
- cline-telemetry\[.\]io C2

## Source notes
GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7; Cline GitHub github.com/cline/cline. Related to ClawHavoc and other malicious OpenClaw skill campaigns. Detection: alert on npm packages with postinstall scripts installing to ~/.openclaw/skills/, check for cline-telemetry[.]io domain, monitor AI credential file access from unexpected processes.

## Sources
- [GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7: Malicious code in cline-cli npm package](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9ppg-jx86-fqw7)
- [Cline - AI coding assistant CLI](https://github.com/cline/cline)

# ShareLeak Copilot Studio SharePoint form prompt injection (CVE-2026-21520)

- ID: shareleak-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520
- Reported: 2026-01-15
- AI role: ai_agent_or_mcp_as_target
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/shareleak-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520/

## Summary
SharePoint-form content could prompt-inject Copilot Studio agents to override behavior and exfiltrate SharePoint data. Microsoft patched 2026-01-15 as CVE-2026-21520.

## Category
attacks-on-ai

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: unknown
- Victims and sectors: unknown
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: Patched Jan 15 2026

## Attack flow
### step-1: Initial delivery details are undisclosed (unknown)

The supplied record identifies form content as the injection channel.

Evidence: <https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/shareleak-taking-the-wheel-of-microsofts-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520>

### step-2: SharePoint form carries instructions (access)

Attacker-controlled form content reaches a Copilot Studio agent.

Evidence: <https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/shareleak-taking-the-wheel-of-microsofts-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520>

### step-3: Prompt injection redirects the agent (ai)

The agent is induced to override its intended behavior.

Evidence: <https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/shareleak-taking-the-wheel-of-microsofts-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520>

### step-4: SharePoint data is exfiltrated (impact)

The reported chain crosses the connector’s data-access boundary.

Evidence: <https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/shareleak-taking-the-wheel-of-microsofts-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0051.001](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.001) Indirect — SharePoint form content redirects the agent.
  Evidence: <https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/shareleak-taking-the-wheel-of-microsofts-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520>
- [AML.T0057](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0057) LLM Data Leakage — The injected behavior leaks SharePoint data.
  Evidence: <https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/shareleak-taking-the-wheel-of-microsofts-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520>

## Prevention
Patch Copilot Studio; treat SharePoint form fields as untrusted prompt input

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in ShareLeak Copilot Studio SharePoint form prompt injection (CVE-2026-21520). Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- [Microsoft Copilot Studio](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/products/copilot-studio)
- SharePoint

### Other tooling
- unknown

## Source notes
unknown

## Sources
- <https://www.capsulesecurity.io/blog-post/shareleak-taking-the-wheel-of-microsofts-copilot-studio-cve-2026-21520>

# Malicious Chrome extensions steal ChatGPT and DeepSeek chats

- ID: ox-security-chrome-ext-chatgpt-deepseek-2025
- Reported: 2025-12-01
- AI role: ai_tool_as_lure
- Entry: https://openattacks.ai/attacks/ox-security-chrome-ext-chatgpt-deepseek-2025/

## Summary
AITOPIA-impersonating Chrome extensions stole ChatGPT and DeepSeek conversation content plus browsing URLs. Reported impact over 900,000 users for related malicious AI-themed extensions in the campaign cluster.

## Category
adversary-use-of-ai

## Attribution
unknown

## AI involvement confidence
confirmed

## Scope and targeting
- Initial access: Victims install malicious Chrome Web Store extensions
- Victims and sectors: unknown
- Regions: unknown
- Region notes: unknown
- Scale and metrics: 900,000+ users cited for related extension cluster

## Attack flow
### step-1: Impersonating extension is installed (access)

A Chrome Web Store extension presents itself as an AI assistant product.

Evidence: <https://www.ox.security/blog/malicious-chrome-extensions-steal-chatgpt-deepseek-conversations/>

### step-2: Extension accesses AI conversations (ai)

The malicious extension reads ChatGPT and DeepSeek chat content.

Evidence: <https://www.ox.security/blog/malicious-chrome-extensions-steal-chatgpt-deepseek-conversations/>

### step-3: Chats and browsing URLs are collected (execution)

The reported behavior includes conversation and browser activity theft.

Evidence: <https://www.ox.security/blog/malicious-chrome-extensions-steal-chatgpt-deepseek-conversations/>

### step-4: Conversation content is stolen (impact)

The campaign affects a large population of extension users.

Evidence: <https://www.ox.security/blog/malicious-chrome-extensions-steal-chatgpt-deepseek-conversations/>

### Connections

- step-1 -> step-2
- step-2 -> step-3
- step-3 -> step-4

## MITRE ATLAS
- [AML.T0085](https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0085) Data from AI Services — Malicious extensions collect conversation content from AI services.
  Evidence: <https://www.ox.security/blog/malicious-chrome-extensions-steal-chatgpt-deepseek-conversations/>

## Prevention
Extension allowlists; review ChatGPT/DeepSeek sessions after removal

## Detections
- Review attack-specific indicators (guidance) — Monitor for the techniques described in Malicious Chrome extensions steal ChatGPT and DeepSeek chats. Refer to sources for specific IOCs and TTPs.

## Timeline
No timeline is recorded.

## Tools
### AI tooling and models
- Fake AI productivity Chrome extensions

### Other tooling
- unknown

## Source notes
unknown

- <https://www.ox.security/blog/malicious-chrome-extensions-steal-chatgpt-deepseek-conversations/>
